**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Jordan Vickers, Associate, Charleston Office

**FROM:** Catherine \"Kit\" Ashworth, Partner, Real Estate Practice Group Chair

**DATE:** March 18, 2025

**RE: Markup Notes --- Template SC Commercial Mortgage and Security Agreement for Calverley Heritage Bank / Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC Loan (\$14,750,000) --- 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403**

Jordan --- I\'ve reviewed our firm\'s standard South Carolina commercial mortgage template against the executed term sheet, title commitment (PT-2025-04-1178), borrower\'s operating agreement summary, rent roll and lease abstracts, and the Phase I ESA executive summary from Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Below are my section-by-section notes and redline comments for your use in preparing the initial draft. Please address each item and flag anything you cannot resolve for discussion at our Wednesday call with Marcus Prideaux at Calverley Heritage Bank. Target delivery of first draft to the client is April 1, 2025, for a projected closing of April 15, 2025.

**[1. Recitals and Defined Terms]{.underline}**

Customize the template recitals as follows. The borrower\'s full legal name is Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company (SC SOS Filing No. 2024-0011287), with its principal office at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, SC 29401. The lender is Calverley Heritage Bank, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank, with its principal office at 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, GA 31401.

The loan amount is **\$14,750,000**. Note the bifurcated structure --- the initial advance is \$12,500,000 at closing and the renovation holdback is \$2,250,000. Define both **\"Initial Advance\"** and **\"Renovation Holdback\"** separately in the definitions section, and describe the conditions for disbursement of the holdback by cross-reference to the renovation disbursement provisions in the mortgage body.

The recitals should reference each Loan Document by name: the Promissory Note, the Guaranty Agreement (from Neil Ashford Graydon), the Environmental Indemnity Agreement, and the Assignment of Leases and Rents. On that last point --- I prefer incorporating the assignment of rents into the mortgage body rather than executing it as a separate instrument for this deal. That approach reduces recording costs and streamlines enforcement. See my detailed notes below in Section 3.

Define **\"Property\"** broadly to include all three tax parcels (460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009) and the vacated Anson Lane strip. Define **\"Loan Documents\"** to cross-reference the GC contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC (SC License No. SC-GC-47921), the renovation budget, and all reserve agreements. Define **\"Guarantor\"** as Neil Ashford Graydon, individually, of 14 Church Street, Charleston, SC 29401. Define **\"Maturity Date\"** as April 15, 2030.

**[2. Granting Clause and Legal Description]{.underline}**

Use the legal description from the title commitment issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective date February 28, 2025, underwritten by Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc.): Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina, together with the former Anson Lane strip vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the aforesaid RMC Office.

**CRITICAL --- ANSON LANE CHAIN OF TITLE.** Jordan --- the Anson Lane strip was conveyed to the borrower\'s predecessor by quitclaim deed only (Deed Book 1128, Page 443). A quitclaim deed provides no warranties of title whatsoever. We need to verify three things before we can be comfortable with this parcel as mortgaged collateral: (1) that the title commitment from Prestige Title and Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc. affirmatively insures fee simple title to the Anson Lane strip without any Schedule B-II exception that carves it out or qualifies the estate as less than fee simple; (2) that the vesting chain from the City of Charleston through the quitclaim deed to the current seller and then to borrower is complete and unbroken, with no gaps in ownership or intervening claims; and (3) whether we should request a specific title endorsement --- an ALTA 9 endorsement or equivalent --- covering this parcel separately to ensure the lender has specific affirmative insurance against loss arising from a title defect in the strip. Review the title commitment Schedule B-II carefully. If the Anson Lane strip is excepted, shown as less than fee simple, or qualified in any way, we have a gap in collateral coverage. This is a non-trivial issue because the strip connects Lots 7 through 9 and its loss could impair vehicular and pedestrian access to the Property and undermine the approved site plan. Flag this for Prestige Title immediately and copy me on any correspondence.

The granting clause should convey a mortgage lien on fee simple title to the Property, together with all improvements now or hereafter erected thereon, all fixtures, building systems, equipment, and appurtenances. Include the standard \"together with\" language for rents, profits, issues, and all other collateral described in the mortgage. Reference all three tax map numbers in the granting clause itself, in addition to the full metes and bounds description in Exhibit A.

Note: The legal description should be set out in **Exhibit A** to the mortgage and referenced in the granting clause by incorporation. We will need the surveyor\'s legal description (metes and bounds) in addition to the plat reference --- confirm with the borrower\'s surveyor that the ALTA/NSPS survey has been ordered and will be delivered in certified form before the closing date.

**[3. Assignment of Leases, Rents, and Profits]{.underline}**

**IMPORTANT --- ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT REQUIRED.** Our template currently uses a collateral assignment of rents, which is the older approach and is insufficient for this deal. South Carolina enacted the Uniform Assignment of Rents Act (S.C. Code § 29-3-100 *et seq.*), and we need to draft this provision as an **absolute assignment** of all leases, rents, issues, and profits of the Property, not merely a collateral assignment. Under the SC statute, an absolute assignment is effective upon execution and recording; the lender\'s right to collect rents is perfected upon recording in the county land records but enforcement --- meaning actual collection of rents by the lender --- is triggered only by borrower default. Revise the template language throughout to remove any \"collateral\" or \"as additional security\" characterization and replace it with \"absolute and present\" assignment language. The operative provision should state affirmatively that borrower unconditionally and absolutely transfers and assigns to Lender all right, title, and interest in and to all current and future leases, subleases, and occupancy agreements affecting the Property, and all rents, income, revenues, issues, profits, and other sums now or hereafter payable thereunder, without reservation.

**CRITICAL --- LOWCOUNTRY PROVISIONS LEASE --- NO ASSIGNMENT/CONSENT CLAUSE.** I\'ve reviewed the lease abstracts from the rent roll in detail. The Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease (Bay 1, approximately 3,800 SF, \$28.50/SF NNN, lease expiration December 31, 2027) has no assignment or subletting provision whatsoever --- the lease abstract notes \"Assignment/Subletting: No provision.\" This is unusual for a commercial lease and creates a significant wrinkle. Under S.C. Code § 29-3-100 *et seq.*, the assignment of rents is enforceable against a tenant upon notification regardless of what the underlying lease says about assignment, so we are legally covered from a pure enforceability standpoint. However, a tenant whose lease contains no express consent-to-assignment clause could raise practical objections or withhold cooperation at the very moment we need to enforce --- and the last thing the bank wants in a workout is a tenant claiming it didn\'t consent to paying rent to the lender.

Best practice here requires three steps: **(a)** require borrower to represent and warrant in the mortgage that it has the full right and authority to assign all rents under all leases affecting the Property, including specifically and without limitation the Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease; **(b)** require delivery of a **tenant estoppel certificate** from Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a condition precedent to closing, in which the tenant acknowledges the existence of the mortgage, the assignment of rents to the lender, and agrees to pay rent to the lender upon written notice following a borrower default; and **(c)** include a post-closing covenant requiring borrower to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a lease amendment to the Lowcountry Provisions lease adding a standard assignment-consent provision at the next renewal, extension, or amendment opportunity. Flag this item for Marcus at the bank --- he should know that the Lowcountry Provisions estoppel is critical and should not be waived.

The other two occupied leases are lower-risk on this point but still require estoppels at closing:

> • **Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC** (Bay 3, approximately 3,800 SF, \$24.00/SF modified gross, lease expiration June 30, 2026) --- the lease abstract shows a standard landlord assignment consent clause. Estoppel required at closing but lower risk.
>
> • **Tidemark Consulting Group LLC** (2nd Floor Suite A, approximately 9,800 SF, \$22.00/SF NNN, lease expiration March 31, 2029) --- same, standard consent-to-assignment provision in the lease. Estoppel required at closing.

The mortgage should grant borrower a revocable license to collect rents until the occurrence and continuance of an Event of Default. Upon default, lender may collect rents directly upon written notice to tenants without the necessity of obtaining a court order or appointing a receiver, though we should also include the standard provisions for lender\'s right to seek appointment of a receiver in any judicial proceeding to enforce the mortgage.

**[4. Single-Purpose Entity Covenants]{.underline}**

**CRITICAL --- SPE COVENANTS VS. OPERATING AGREEMENT.** The term sheet requires full single-purpose entity covenants for Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC. I\'ve reviewed the redacted summary of the borrower\'s operating agreement provided by borrower\'s counsel, and it does **not** currently contain any of the following provisions, all of which we will need:

**(1) Independent Director/Manager Requirement.** The operating agreement designates Graydon Development Group LLC as the sole managing member with exclusive management authority. There is no provision whatsoever for an independent director or independent manager whose affirmative consent is required before the borrower may file a voluntary bankruptcy petition, consent to an involuntary bankruptcy petition, dissolve, merge, consolidate, or wind up its affairs. We need this provision for bankruptcy remoteness --- without it, Graydon Development Group LLC could unilaterally file the borrower into bankruptcy, which defeats the entire purpose of the SPE structure.

**(2) Separateness Covenants.** The operating agreement does not include standard separateness covenants. We need the borrower to covenant that it shall at all times: maintain separate books and records; maintain separate bank accounts; not commingle its assets with those of any affiliate; hold itself out to the public as a separate legal entity; use its own stationery, invoices, and checks; not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any affiliate; pay its own liabilities from its own assets; maintain arm\'s-length relationships with affiliates; and maintain adequate capitalization in light of its contemplated business.

**(3) Restriction to Single Purpose.** The operating agreement\'s purpose clause appears to allow \"any lawful business\" --- a standard boilerplate formulation. We need this narrowed to a single-purpose restriction: the borrower\'s sole purpose is owning, operating, managing, leasing, and financing the Property at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403, and activities incidental thereto.

**(4) Member Consent.** Here is the complication. The borrower has three members with potentially divergent economic and governance interests: **Graydon Development Group LLC** (72% membership interest), **Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP** (18% membership interest), and **Harborline Capital Advisors LLC** (10% membership interest). The SPE covenants --- especially the independent director requirement and the restriction on voluntary bankruptcy filings --- must be binding on all members, not just the managing member. We need written confirmation that Tidewater and Harborline have reviewed the SPE restrictions, understand their implications, and have consented to be bound by them. The operating agreement summary I reviewed does not reflect any such consent.

**ACTION ITEMS:**

> \(a\) Draft the SPE covenants in the mortgage as though the operating agreement already contains compliant provisions --- that is, include representations and warranties that the borrower\'s organizational documents contain SPE provisions satisfying the lender\'s requirements.
>
> \(b\) Separately, prepare a form of **Operating Agreement Amendment** adding the independent director requirement, separateness covenants, single-purpose restriction, and unanimity requirement for bankruptcy filings, dissolution, and merger.
>
> \(c\) Make delivery of the executed Operating Agreement Amendment --- signed by **all three members** (Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC) --- a **condition precedent to closing**.
>
> \(d\) Include a covenant in the mortgage that borrower shall not amend, modify, or waive any SPE provision of its operating agreement without the lender\'s prior written consent in each instance.

One additional note: **Tidewater GP Holdings LLC** is the general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP. Confirm that Tidewater GP Holdings LLC has the authority to bind the fund to the operating agreement amendment. Check the limited partnership agreement or, if that is not available, request a GP authorization certificate or resolution prior to closing.

**[5. Prepayment / Yield Maintenance]{.underline}**

The prepayment structure from the term sheet is as follows: a 24-month absolute lockout period (months 1--24), followed by yield maintenance (months 25--48), followed by open prepayment with no premium (months 49--60, i.e., the final 12 months before the April 15, 2030 Maturity Date).

**CRITICAL --- YIELD MAINTENANCE FORMULA MUST BE PRECISE.** The term sheet describes the prepayment premium as \"yield maintenance (treasury rate + 50 bps spread)\" but does not specify several critical variables, each of which must be defined with precision in the mortgage:

> **(a)** Which U.S. Treasury rate? The Constant Maturity Treasury (CMT) rate? If so, for what tenor --- matched to the remaining term of the loan from the prepayment date to maturity? Matched to the remaining yield maintenance period? Interpolated between two published tenors if no exact match exists?
>
> **(b)** How is the present value of remaining payments calculated? Is the discount rate the Treasury rate alone, or the Treasury rate plus the 50 basis point spread referenced in the term sheet?
>
> **(c)** Is the prepayment premium the greater of the yield maintenance amount or some fixed minimum percentage of the prepaid principal (e.g., 1%), or is it the yield maintenance amount standing alone with no minimum?
>
> **(d)** What happens if the calculated yield maintenance premium is zero or negative --- that is, if Treasury rates have risen sufficiently since origination that there is no present-value differential? Is there a floor of zero, or is there a minimum premium regardless?

**South Carolina enforceability concern.** SC courts have generally enforced yield maintenance premiums in commercial loan transactions as reasonable liquidated damages provisions, but the formula must be specific, mathematically deterministic, and objectively calculable at the time of prepayment. If the formula is ambiguous or requires subjective judgment calls, a court could deem it an unenforceable penalty or refuse to enforce it on grounds of indefiniteness. We dealt with precisely this issue in a prior transaction approximately two years ago, and I do not want a repeat.

**DRAFTING INSTRUCTION.** Insert a precise, self-contained yield maintenance formula in the mortgage substantially as follows:

> *\"The Yield Maintenance Premium shall equal the positive excess, if any, of (A) the present value of all remaining scheduled monthly payments of interest and principal from the prepayment date through the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period (the payment due on or about month 48 following the date of the Note), discounted monthly at a per annum rate equal to the Treasury Rate, over (B) the outstanding principal amount being prepaid. The \"Treasury Rate\" shall mean the yield to maturity, as of the second Business Day preceding the prepayment date, of the United States Treasury security (as reported in Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15 --- Selected Interest Rates, or any successor publication) having a maturity date closest to, but not exceeding, the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period. If no published maturity exactly matches, interpolate linearly between the two nearest published maturities. In no event shall the Yield Maintenance Premium be less than zero.\"*

A key interpretive question: the 50 basis points referenced in the term sheet. Add the 50 bps to the **loan rate** (not to the Treasury rate) when computing the stream of remaining payments to be discounted --- that is, the remaining payments should be calculated at the Note rate, and the spread over Treasuries reflects the lender\'s bargained-for return. Confirm this interpretation with Marcus before finalizing. The term sheet\'s reference to \"treasury rate + 50 bps spread\" is ambiguous on its face and could reasonably be read either way.

Include the lockout provision as an **absolute prohibition** on voluntary prepayment during months 1 through 24, with no exception other than the application of casualty insurance proceeds or condemnation awards, which should be applied at par without any prepayment premium. Confirm this casualty/condemnation carve-out with the client --- some lenders want a premium even on involuntary prepayments, though that is the minority position.

**[6. Additional Notes --- Other Sections Requiring Attention]{.underline}**

The following sections of the template require customization but are more straightforward. Brief notes on each:

**Security Interest / UCC Collateral. Standard Article 9 language. Ensure we cover all personal property, fixtures (file as a fixture filing in the Charleston County RMC and as a UCC-1 financing statement with the SC Secretary of State), equipment, accounts, general intangibles, insurance proceeds, condemnation proceeds, permits, licenses, contracts (including the GC contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC), and all reserve accounts held by the lender. The UCC-1 should name Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC (EIN: 84-6213750) as debtor and Calverley Heritage Bank as secured party. Confirm the collateral description in the UCC-1 matches the mortgage.**

**Renovation Disbursement Provisions.** The holdback is \$2,250,000 against a total renovation budget of \$3,150,000 --- the term sheet contemplates periodic draws from the holdback upon satisfaction of disbursement conditions. Build in standard draw procedures: written draw request with not less than ten business days\' advance notice, architect\'s certification of percentage completion, unconditional lien waivers from Beaufort Builders Group LLC and all subcontractors for all work covered by prior draws, a title endorsement (no intervening liens since last draw), and 10% retainage until substantial completion. Substantial completion deadline is June 15, 2026. Cross-reference the completion guaranty from Neil Ashford Graydon, which guarantees the borrower\'s obligation to complete the renovation on budget and on schedule.

**Insurance Covenants.** Standard commercial property coverage: all-risk (special form) at full replacement cost, commercial general liability (\$2,000,000 per occurrence / \$5,000,000 aggregate), builder\'s risk during the renovation period, and the reserve/escrow provisions for insurance premiums. The template should be fine here --- just update the coverage amounts and add the builder\'s risk requirement for the construction phase.

**Financial Covenants.** DSCR minimum of 1.25x, tested quarterly on a trailing twelve-month basis, beginning 24 months post-closing (first test date April 15, 2027). Guarantor minimum net worth of not less than \$1,000,000, tested annually. Guarantor minimum liquid assets of not less than \$500,000, tested annually. Audited financial statements of borrower within 120 days of fiscal year end. Quarterly rent rolls within 30 days of each calendar quarter end. These are all specified in the term sheet --- populate the template accordingly.

**Default and Remedies.** Standard default provisions. Ensure we include SC-specific foreclosure language --- South Carolina is a judicial foreclosure state with no power of sale. The mortgage should not purport to grant a power of sale. Cross-default to the Note, the Guaranty Agreement, and the Environmental Indemnity Agreement. Default rate of interest: the applicable rate plus 5.00% per annum. Late charge: 5% of any installment of principal or interest not received within 10 calendar days of its due date.

**Governing Law / Recording.** South Carolina law governs. The mortgage will be recorded in the Charleston County Register of Mesne Conveyance. Confirm documentary stamp tax and recording fee calculations with Prestige Title before closing. The mortgage tax in South Carolina is 0.37% of the indebtedness secured --- on \$14,750,000, that is \$54,575.00. Budget accordingly.

**Environmental Covenants.** Use our standard template environmental compliance covenant. The Phase I ESA from Clearfield Environmental Consulting came back clean except for the controlled recognized environmental condition, which has a no-further-action letter on file. The Environmental Indemnity Agreement is a separate document executed by borrower and guarantor and will handle the substantive environmental risk allocation. Standard provisions in the mortgage should suffice.

**[Closing Notes]{.underline}**

Jordan --- let me know if you have questions on any of the foregoing. Prioritize the assignment of rents restructuring (switching from collateral to absolute assignment), the SPE/operating agreement issue (including the form of operating agreement amendment), and the yield maintenance formula. Those are the three most complex drafting tasks and I want to see them handled correctly in the first draft. I want to see a clean initial draft by **March 28** so we have time for internal review before sending to Marcus on April 1.

Also, do not forget to confirm the Anson Lane chain of title with Prestige Title early in the process --- if there is a gap in the title to that strip, we need to know well before we get deep into document drafting and negotiate ourselves into a corner.

One more thought --- coordinate with Marcus on whether the bank\'s loan committee or board has approved any exceptions to standard underwriting guidelines for this loan. The as-is LTV runs a little hot. He\'ll know what I mean.

Kit

Catherine \"Kit\" Ashworth Partner Fielding, Ashworth & Cole LLP Charleston & Savannah

for k,v in rents.items(): print(k, cf(v))
tot=sum(rents.values()); print("Total in-place rent:", cf(tot), "| stated $415,100 -> ", "MATCH" if abs(tot-415100)<1 else "MISMATCH")

occ_sf=3800+3800+9800; vac_sf=3800+9800

low = 28.50*1.03  # Jan 1 2025

print(cf(18050+15200+35933), "stated $69,183")
print()
print("=== LOAN METRICS ===")
L=14750000; val=18200000; stab=23500000; cost=20950000

print("Total project cost:", cf(17800000+3150000))
print("Equity:", cf(6200000), "=", f"{6200000/cost:.4%}", "of TPC")
print("Sources: 14,750,000 + 6,200,000 =", cf(L+6200000), "vs uses", cf(cost))
print("Purchase equity: 17,800,000 - 12,500,000 =", cf(5300000), "+ reno equity 900,000 =", cf(6200000))
print("Holdback:", cf(L-12500000))
print()
print("=== RENOVATION BUDGET ===")
b={"HVAC":1200000,"Elev":475000,"Facade":625000,"TI":550000,"Soft+Cont":300000}
print("Sum:", cf(sum(b.values())), "| hard (GC contract):", cf(sum(list(b.values())[:4])), "(stated 2,850,000)")
print("Holdback 2,250,000 vs GC contract 2,850,000 -> gap", cf(2850000-2250000), "=", f"{2250000/2850000:.2%}", "of hard costs covered")
print("Holdback % of total budget:", f"{2250000/3150000:.4%}", "| equity %:", f"{900000/3150000:.4%}")
print("Holdback alloc: 850+375+425+450+150 =", 850000+375000+425000+450000+150000)
print("Equity alloc: 350+100+200+100+150 =", 350000+100000+200000+100000+150000)
print("TI allowance per SF on 13,600 SF:", cf(550000/13600))
print()
print("=== RESERVES / FEES ===")
print("Cap replacement: 0.25*31000 =", cf(0.25*31000), "/yr; monthly", cf(0.25*31000/12))
print("Origination 1%:", cf(0.01*L))

{"command": "mkdir -p $WORKSPACE_DIR/build && cat > $WORKSPACE_DIR/build/docbuilder.py << 'PYEOF'
import re, sys
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

FONT = "Times New Roman"

def add_field(paragraph, instr):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fld = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin'); run._r.append(fld)
    run2 = paragraph.add_run()
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); it.text = instr; run2._r.append(it)
    run3 = paragraph.add_run()
    fld2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'separate'); run3._r.append(fld2)
    run4 = paragraph.add_run("1")
    run5 = paragraph.add_run()
    fld3 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld3.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end'); run5._r.append(fld3)
    for r in (run, run2, run3, run4, run5):
        r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)

def style_doc(doc):
    st = doc.styles['Normal']
    st.font.name = FONT; st.font.size = Pt(11)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), FONT)
    pf = st.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(0); pf.space_after = Pt(8)
    pf.line_spacing_rule = WD_LINE_SPACING.SINGLE
    for s in doc.sections:
        s.top_margin = Inches(1.0); s.bottom_margin = Inches(1.0)
        s.left_margin = Inches(1.0); s.right_margin = Inches(1.0)

def add_runs(p, text, base_bold=False, size=None, caps=False):
    # supports **bold** and *italic*
    tokens = re.split(r'(\*\*[^*]+\*\*|\*[^*]+\*)', text)
    for t in tokens:
        if not t: continue
        if t.startswith('**') and t.endswith('**'):
            r = p.add_run(t[2:-2]); r.bold = True
        elif t.startswith('*') and t.endswith('*') and len(t) > 2:
            r = p.add_run(t[1:-1]); r.italic = True
        else:
            r = p.add_run(t); r.bold = base_bold
        r.font.name = FONT
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if caps: r.font.all_caps = True

def build(content_path, out_path, header_text=None, footer_label="", title_page=None):
    doc = Document()
    style_doc(doc)
    # header / footer
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    if header_text:
        hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
        hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r = hp.add_run(header_text); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(8.5); r.italic = True
    fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    if footer_label:
        r = fp.add_run(footer_label + "   |   Page "); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)
    else:
        r = fp.add_run("Page "); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)
    add_field(fp, "PAGE")
    r = fp.add_run(" of "); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)
    add_field(fp, "NUMPAGES")

    lines = open(content_path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    i = 0
    pending_table = None
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i].rstrip()
        i += 1
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^\[([A-Z0-9]+)\]\s?(.*)$', line)
        if not m:
            # continuation of previous? treat as [P]
            tag, text = 'P', line
        else:
            tag, text = m.group(1), m.group(2)

        if tag == 'TITLE':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(120)
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True, size=22)
        elif tag == 'SUBTITLE':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(10); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(10)
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True, size=13)
        elif tag == 'C':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'CB':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True)
        elif tag == 'CSM':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            for r in p.runs: pass
            rr = p.add_run(text); rr.font.name = FONT; rr.font.size = Pt(9.5); rr.italic = True
        elif tag == 'A':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(16); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(10)
            p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True, size=11.5)
        elif tag == 'H':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(8); p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(0.0)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'P':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == '1':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.5)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.25)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == '2':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(1.0)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.25)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'SIG':
            p = doc.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(3.0)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'SIGL':
            p = doc.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'PB':
            doc.add_page_break()
        elif tag == 'GAP':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        elif tag == 'T':
            # table caption already handled; start collecting rows
            rows = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith('[R]'):
                rows.append([c.strip() for c in lines[i][3:].split('|')])
                i += 1
            ncols = max(len(r) for r in rows)
            table = doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=ncols)
            table.style = 'Table Grid'
            table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
            for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
                cells = table.add_row().cells
                for ci in range(ncols):
                    txt = row[ci] if ci < len(row) else ''
                    cp = cells[ci].paragraphs[0]
                    cp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
                    cp.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
                    if ri == 0:
                        add_runs(cp, txt, base_bold=True, size=9.5)
                    else:
                        add_runs(cp, txt, size=9.5)

import re, sys
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

FONT = "Times New Roman"

def add_field(paragraph, instr):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fld = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin'); run._r.append(fld)
    run2 = paragraph.add_run()
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); it.text = instr; run2._r.append(it)
    run3 = paragraph.add_run()
    fld2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'separate'); run3._r.append(fld2)
    run4 = paragraph.add_run("1")
    run5 = paragraph.add_run()
    fld3 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld3.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end'); run5._r.append(fld3)
    for r in (run, run2, run3, run4, run5):
        r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)

def style_doc(doc):
    st = doc.styles['Normal']
    st.font.name = FONT; st.font.size = Pt(11)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), FONT)
    pf = st.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(0); pf.space_after = Pt(8)
    pf.line_spacing_rule = WD_LINE_SPACING.SINGLE
    for s in doc.sections:
        s.top_margin = Inches(1.0); s.bottom_margin = Inches(1.0)
        s.left_margin = Inches(1.0); s.right_margin = Inches(1.0)

def add_runs(p, text, base_bold=False, size=None, caps=False):
    # supports **bold** and *italic*
    tokens = re.split(r'(\*\*[^*]+\*\*|\*[^*]+\*)', text)
    for t in tokens:
        if not t: continue
        if t.startswith('**') and t.endswith('**'):
            r = p.add_run(t[2:-2]); r.bold = True
        elif t.startswith('*') and t.endswith('*') and len(t) > 2:
            r = p.add_run(t[1:-1]); r.italic = True
        else:
            r = p.add_run(t); r.bold = base_bold
        r.font.name = FONT
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if caps: r.font.all_caps = True

def build(content_path, out_path, header_text=None, footer_label="", title_page=None):
    doc = Document()
    style_doc(doc)
    # header / footer
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    if header_text:
        hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
        hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r = hp.add_run(header_text); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(8.5); r.italic = True
    fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    if footer_label:
        r = fp.add_run(footer_label + "   |   Page "); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)
    else:
        r = fp.add_run("Page "); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)
    add_field(fp, "PAGE")
    r = fp.add_run(" of "); r.font.name = FONT; r.font.size = Pt(9)
    add_field(fp, "NUMPAGES")

    lines = open(content_path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    i = 0
    pending_table = None
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i].rstrip()
        i += 1
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^\[([A-Z0-9]+)\]\s?(.*)$', line)
        if not m:
            # continuation of previous? treat as [P]
            tag, text = 'P', line
        else:
            tag, text = m.group(1), m.group(2)

        if tag == 'TITLE':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(120)
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True, size=22)
        elif tag == 'SUBTITLE':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(10); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(10)
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True, size=13)
        elif tag == 'C':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'CB':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True)
        elif tag == 'CSM':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            for r in p.runs: pass
            rr = p.add_run(text); rr.font.name = FONT; rr.font.size = Pt(9.5); rr.italic = True
        elif tag == 'A':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(16); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(10)
            p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
            add_runs(p, text, base_bold=True, size=11.5)
        elif tag == 'H':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(8); p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(0.0)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'P':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == '1':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.5)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.25)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == '2':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(1.0)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.25)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'SIG':
            p = doc.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(3.0)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'SIGL':
            p = doc.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, text)
        elif tag == 'PB':
            doc.add_page_break()
        elif tag == 'GAP':
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        elif tag == 'T':
            # table caption already handled; start collecting rows
            rows = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith('[R]'):
                rows.append([c.strip() for c in lines[i][3:].split('|')])
                i += 1
            ncols = max(len(r) for r in rows)
            table = doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=ncols)
            table.style = 'Table Grid'
            table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
            for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
                cells = table.add_row().cells
                for ci in range(ncols):
                    txt = row[ci] if ci < len(row) else ''
                    cp = cells[ci].paragraphs[0]
                    cp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
                    cp.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
                    if ri == 0:
                        add_runs(cp, txt, base_bold=True, size=9.5)
                    else:
                        add_runs(cp, txt, size=9.5)
            # spacing after table
            sp = doc.add_paragraph(); sp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
        else:
            p = doc.add_paragraph(); add_runs(p, text)

    doc.save(out_path)
    print("saved", out_path)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    build(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv)>3 else None,
          sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv)>4 else "")

[1](a) one percent (1.00%) of the principal amount of the Loan outstanding on the Prepayment Date; and
[1](b) the present value, determined as of the Prepayment Date, of the excess, if any, of (i) the aggregate amount of interest that would have accrued on the principal amount prepaid, computed at the rate of interest in effect under the Note on the Prepayment Date, for the period from the Prepayment Date through the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period, over (ii) the aggregate amount of interest that would have accrued on such principal amount for the same period, computed at a per annum rate equal to the Treasury Rate plus fifty (50) basis points (0.50%).

[H]**4.8 Involuntary Prepayments.** Amounts applied to the Indebtedness as a result of a casualty or a Condemnation in accordance with Article XI shall be applied at par, without any prepayment premium or Yield Maintenance Premium, and shall be applied in the order of application set forth in Section 13.8. [H]**4.10 Late Charge.** If any installment of principal, interest or other amount due under the Loan Documents is not received by Lender within ten (10) calendar days after the date on which it is due, Borrower shall pay to Lender on demand a late charge equal to five percent (5.00%) of the overdue amount. The late charge is intended to compensate Lender for the additional administrative expense of processing delinquent payments and is not a penalty, and it is payable in addition to, and not in lieu of, interest at the Default Rate. The imposition of a late charge shall not cure any payment default, shall not extend any cure period, and shall not constitute a waiver of any Event of Default.
[H]**4.11 Default Rate.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan and, to the extent permitted by law, all other amounts due under the Loan Documents, shall bear interest at the Default Rate, from the date of the occurrence of such Event of Default until such Event of Default is cured or the Loan is repaid in full, whichever first occurs. [H]**4.12 Interest Rate Limitation.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no provision of this Mortgage or any other Loan Document shall require the payment or permit the collection of interest in excess of the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, and if any excess is received, it shall be applied to principal or refunded to Borrower.

[P]For purposes of clause (b), the differential described above shall be computed on a monthly basis over the number of full and partial months remaining in the Yield Maintenance Period (each such month being treated as one-twelfth of a year and each partial month being prorated on the basis of a 30-day month and a 360-day year), and each monthly amount shall be discounted to present value as of the Prepayment Date at a monthly discount rate equal to the Treasury Rate divided by twelve (12), using the formula P = A ÷ (1 + r)^n, where "P" is the present value of each monthly amount, "A" is such monthly amount, "r" is the Treasury Rate divided by twelve (12), and "n" is the number of months from the Prepayment Date to the date on which such amount would have accrued. The Yield Maintenance Premium shall in no event be less than the amount determined under clause (a), and in no event shall any circumstance result in a Yield Maintenance Premium of less than zero.
[P]Borrower acknowledges that the Yield Maintenance Premium is intended to compensate Lender for the loss of the benefit of its bargain resulting from the prepayment of a fixed-spread, floating-rate obligation at a time when interest rates have declined, that such loss is difficult if not impossible to calculate with precision, and that the Yield Maintenance Premium is a reasonable estimate of such loss and constitutes liquidated damages and not a penalty. Borrower waives, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any defense to the enforcement of the Yield Maintenance Premium based on the assertion that it is a penalty, unconscionable, or an unreasonable estimate of Lender's loss. Lender shall provide Borrower with a written calculation of the Yield Maintenance Premium within five (5) Business Days after request, which calculation shall be conclusive absent manifest error.
[H]**4.6 Open Prepayment Period.** At any time during the final twelve (12) months of the term of the Loan (that is, from and after the expiration of the Yield Maintenance Period through the Maturity Date), Borrower may prepay the Loan in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time, without payment of any prepayment premium, penalty or yield maintenance amount, upon not less than fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Lender specifying the Prepayment Date and the amount to be prepaid. Amounts prepaid in part shall be applied to the outstanding principal balance and shall not reduce or otherwise affect the amount of any scheduled installment of interest or principal thereafter due, except as calculated in accordance with the Note.
[H]**4.7 Ineligible Prepayments.** If Borrower makes any prepayment (a) during the Lockout Period, (b) in part during the Yield Maintenance Period, or (c) otherwise other than in accordance with Sections 4.4 or 4.6, then Borrower shall pay, in addition to the amount prepaid, a prepayment premium equal to the Yield Maintenance Premium determined under Section 4.5 (with the principal amount prepaid being substituted for the principal amount outstanding for purposes of clause (a) thereof), and Lender may, at its option, refuse to accept such payment. Acceptance of any ineligible prepayment shall not constitute a waiver of any Event of Default arising therefrom.
[H]**4.8 Involuntary Prepayments.** Amounts applied to the Indebtedness as a result of a casualty or a Condemnation in accordance with Article XI shall be applied at par, without any prepayment premium or Yield Maintenance Premium, and shall be applied in the order of application set forth in Section 13.8. Lender may, but shall not be obligated to, permit restoration of the Improvements in accordance with Section 11.8.
[H]**4.9 Application of Payments.** All payments received shall be applied in the following order: (a) costs and expenses (including attorneys' fees) incurred by Lender in connection with the enforcement or preservation of its rights; (b) late charges; (c) the Yield Maintenance Premium and any prepayment premium; (d) interest at the Default Rate; (e) interest at the rate otherwise payable under the Note; (f) principal; and (g) all other amounts due under the Loan Documents. Lender may apply payments in any other order it elects in its discretion notwithstanding any designation by Borrower.
[H]**4.10 Late Charge.** If any installment of principal, interest or other amount due under the Loan Documents is not received by Lender within ten (10) calendar days after the date on which it is due, Borrower shall pay to Lender on demand a late charge equal to five percent (5.00%) of the overdue amount. The late charge is intended to compensate Lender for the additional administrative expense of processing delinquent payments and is not a penalty, and it is payable in addition to, and not in lieu of, interest at the Default Rate. The imposition of a late charge shall not cure any payment default, shall not extend any cure period, and shall not constitute a waiver of any Event of Default.
[H]**4.11 Default Rate.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan and, to the extent permitted by law, all other amounts due under the Loan Documents, shall bear interest at the Default Rate, from the date of the occurrence of such Event of Default until such Event of Default is cured or the Loan is repaid in full, whichever first occurs. Interest at the Default Rate shall be payable on demand, shall itself bear interest at the Default Rate if not paid when due, and shall be secured by this Mortgage.
[H]**4.12 Interest Rate Limitation.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no provision of this Mortgage or any other Loan Document shall require the payment or permit the collection of interest in excess of the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, and if any excess is received, it shall be applied to principal or refunded to Borrower.

The execution, delivery and performance of this Mortgage do not and will not (a) violate Borrower's Articles of Organization or Operating Agreement (as amended through the date hereof and as amended by the Operating Agreement Amendment), (b) violate any applicable law, order or judgment, (c) result in the creation of any lien on the Property other than in favor of Lender and the Permitted Exceptions, or (d) constitute a default under any material agreement to which Borrower is a party, including the Construction Contract and the Leases.
[H]**5.3 Title to the Property.** Borrower will, upon recording of the deed described in Section 6.8 and immediately prior to the recording of this Mortgage, be the sole fee simple owner of the Land and the Improvements, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, and will have good and marketable title thereto. Borrower has the full right, power and authority to mortgage the Property and to grant the security interests and assignments provided in this Mortgage.
[H]**5.4 Legal Description; Survey.** The description of the Property set forth in **Exhibit A** is a true, correct and complete description of the Land, including all three (3) tax parcels and the vacated Anson Lane strip, and conforms to the legal description contained in the title commitment issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC, Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective February 28, 2025 (the "**Title Commitment**"), and to the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey of the Property prepared by Cartwright Land Surveying LLC and certified to Lender, the title insurer and Borrower. There are no improvements, encroachments or uses of the Property that are not reflected in such survey, except as disclosed therein or in the Title Commitment.
[H]**5.5 Permitted Exceptions; Encroachment.** The Permitted Exceptions are the only liens, encumbrances, easements, restrictions and other matters affecting the Property, and none of them (other than those disclosed in **Exhibit B**) materially and adversely impairs the use, operation or value of the Property or Lender's security. Borrower acknowledges that a decorative iron balcony extends approximately two and one-half (2.5) feet beyond the front façade of the Improvements over the King Street public right-of-way, and Borrower has not obtained any encroachment agreement, license or permit from the City of Charleston with respect thereto. Borrower has not received any notice from the City of Charleston requiring the removal or modification of such balcony.
[H]**5.6 Leases; Rent Roll.** **Exhibit D** sets forth a true, correct and complete schedule of all Leases affecting the Property as of the date hereof, and the information contained therein concerning the identity of each Tenant, the premises demised, the leasable square footage, the base rent, the escalation provisions, the expiration date, the security deposit held, the renewal options and the assignment, estoppel and SNDA provisions of each Lease is true and correct in all material respects. There are no Leases other than those listed on **Exhibit D**, no Tenant has any option or right of first refusal to purchase all or any portion of the Property, no rent has been prepaid more than one (1) month in advance, and no Tenant is entitled to any concession, free rent, tenant improvement allowance or other inducement that is not disclosed on **Exhibit D**. Borrower acknowledges that the Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC Lease grants that Tenant a Right of First Refusal with respect to Bay 2 of the Property, as disclosed on **Exhibit D**, and that such Right of First Refusal survives renewal of such Lease.
[H]**5.7 Single-Purpose Entity.** On and as of the Closing Date, and after giving effect to the Operating Agreement Amendment delivered at Closing, Borrower is and shall be a Single-Purpose Entity that satisfies each of the requirements of Section 6.7, and Borrower's organizational documents contain the provisions described in Section 6.8. Borrower acknowledges that Lender would not make the Loan on the terms set forth in the Loan Documents but for this representation.
[H]**5.8 No Subordinate Financing; No Other Liens.** Borrower has not incurred, and no Person has any commitment to provide, any indebtedness secured by the Property or any direct or indirect interest in Borrower other than the Loan, and there are no mechanics', materialmen's, judgment, tax or other liens against the Property other than the Permitted Exceptions.
[H]**5.9 Environmental; Land Use Restriction.** Borrower has received and reviewed the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment prepared by Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC, Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025 (the "**Phase I Report**"). Except as disclosed in the Phase I Report, there are no Hazardous Substances (as defined in the Environmental Indemnity Agreement) located on, under, in or emanating from the Property, and no underground or above-ground storage tanks, asbestos-containing materials, polychlorinated biphenyls, lead-based paint or radon in concentrations exceeding applicable standards are present at the Property. Borrower acknowledges that one (1) Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition exists with respect to Lot 7 arising from off-site contamination originating at the adjacent property located at 518 King Street, that such condition was addressed under the oversight of the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control ("**SCDHEC**") with a "No Further Action" determination dated August 12, 2021 (SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772), and that such condition is subject to the recorded land use restriction described in Article VIII. Borrower has not received any notice of any violation of, or any inquiry concerning, the land use restriction or the SCDHEC institutional controls, and to Borrower's knowledge no condition exists that would constitute a breach thereof.
[H]**5.10 Renovation Budget; Construction Contract.** The Renovation Budget attached as **Exhibit C** is true, correct and complete and reflects Borrower's good-faith estimate of the total cost of the Renovation Work. The Construction Contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC (South Carolina General Contractor License No. SC-GC-47921) provides for a contract sum of $2,850,000.00 covering hard costs of construction, and the balance of $300,000.00 for soft costs and contingency is outside the scope of the Construction Contract. A complete and correct copy of the executed Construction Contract, together with all schedules, exhibits, amendments and change orders, has been delivered to Lender. The Construction Contract is in full force and effect, and neither Borrower nor, to Borrower's knowledge, the contractor is in default thereunder.
[H]**5.11 Insurance.** Borrower has obtained, or will obtain prior to the Closing Date, each policy of insurance required by Article XI, and each such policy is or will be in full force and effect, with premiums paid, and names Lender as mortgagee, loss payee and/or additional insured as required.
[H]**5.12 Financial Statements.** All financial statements and other financial information delivered to Lender by Borrower or Guarantor are true, correct and complete in all material respects, have been prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied (except that unaudited statements are subject to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes), and fairly present the financial condition of the Persons to which they relate as of the dates and for the periods indicated. Neither Borrower nor Guarantor has any material contingent liability, guaranty or obligation not disclosed therein.
[H]**5.13 Litigation.** There is no action, suit, proceeding, arbitration, claim or investigation pending or, to Borrower's knowledge, threatened against Borrower or Guarantor that, if adversely determined, could reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on Borrower, Guarantor or the Property, and there is no pending or, to Borrower's knowledge, threatened Condemnation or rezoning proceeding affecting the Property.
[H]**5.14 Compliance with Laws; Zoning.** The Property and its use and operation comply in all material respects with all applicable zoning, building, fire, health, safety, environmental, accessibility and other laws, ordinances, rules and regulations, including the land use restriction described in Article VIII. The Property is located in the GB (General Business) zoning district of the City of Charleston, and the current use of the Property is permitted in such district.
[H]**5.15 Flood Zone.** The Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard) and is not located in a special flood hazard area; no federally mandated flood insurance is required with respect to the Property. Borrower acknowledges that Lender nevertheless requires flood insurance in accordance with Section 11.3.
[H]**5.16 Not a Foreign Person; OFAC; Patriot Act.** Borrower is not a "foreign person" within the meaning of Section 1445 of the Code, and neither Borrower nor any of its members, nor Guarantor, is a person or entity identified on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List maintained by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control, or is otherwise subject to any economic sanctions. Borrower shall comply with all applicable anti-money laundering and know-your-customer requirements.
[H]**5.17 ERISA.** Borrower is not, and the Property does not constitute, a "plan asset" of any employee benefit plan subject to Title I of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended.
[H]**5.18 No Default.** No event has occurred and is continuing that constitutes, or with the giving of notice or lapse of time or both would constitute, an Event of Default.
[H]**5.19 Survival.** The representations and warranties in this Article V shall survive the Closing, the recording of this Mortgage and the making of each Advance, and shall be deemed remade as of the date of each Advance except as otherwise expressly provided.
[A]ARTICLE VI
[A]AFFIRMATIVE COVENANTS
[P]Until the Obligations have been paid and performed in full, Borrower shall, at its sole cost and expense:
[H]**6.1 Impositions.** Pay and discharge, before delinquency and before any interest or penalty attaches, all Impositions and all claims for labor, materials and services that could become a lien on the Property; provided that Borrower may contest in good faith by appropriate proceedings any Imposition or lien, so long as (a) Borrower has deposited with Lender such security as Lender reasonably requires or has provided a bond, (b) such contest suspends collection and prevents the sale or forfeiture of the Property, and (c) Lender's lien and the Property are not otherwise impaired. Borrower shall deliver to Lender receipts or other evidence of payment upon request and, in any event, not later than five (5) Business Days before any Imposition becomes delinquent.
[H]**6.2 Maintenance; Repair; Waste.** Keep and maintain the Property, including the Improvements, all building systems, fixtures, the decorative iron balcony and the vapor barrier beneath the ground-floor slab of Lot 7, in good order, condition and repair, and in at least as good condition as exists on the Closing Date (ordinary wear and tear excepted), consistent with the standards of comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area. Borrower shall not commit or permit any waste of the Property, shall promptly repair or restore any damage not constituting a casualty to be addressed under Article XI, and shall not remove or demolish any material portion of the Improvements without Lender's prior written consent.
[H]**6.3 Compliance with Laws.** Comply, and cause the Property and all Tenants and contractors to comply, with all applicable federal, state and local laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, orders and permits, including all zoning, building, fire, life safety, accessibility, historic preservation, environmental and land use laws, the requirements of the City of Charleston Board of Architectural Review, and the land use restriction described in Article VIII. Borrower shall promptly deliver to Lender copies of all notices of violation or non-compliance received from any governmental authority.
[H]**6.4 Leasing Covenant.** Use commercially reasonable efforts to lease all vacant space at the Property (currently consisting of Bay 2, comprising approximately 3,800 square feet, and Second Floor Suite B, comprising approximately 9,800 square feet) at market rents and on terms consistent with those prevailing for comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area, and on terms reasonably acceptable to Lender. Borrower shall (a) comply with the Right of First Refusal held by Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC with respect to Bay 2 before executing any lease of Bay 2 or entering into any exclusive negotiation with respect thereto, (b) not execute any new Lease or any amendment, extension, renewal or modification of an existing Lease for premises in excess of five thousand (5,000) square feet, or for a term (including all renewal options that Borrower is obligated to grant or that are exercisable at the Tenant's election) exceeding five (5) years, without Lender's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, and (c) deliver to Lender a copy of each Lease and each amendment within ten (10) Business Days after execution.
[H]**6.5 Financial Covenants.** Maintain, at all times during the term of the Loan:
[1](a) a DSCR of not less than 1.25 to 1.00, tested on a trailing twelve (12) month basis, commencing with the first full calendar quarter ending after the twenty-fourth (24th) month following the Closing Date (anticipated to be the calendar quarter ending June 30, 2027, with the first test reported as of July 15, 2027) and quarterly thereafter, and certified by Borrower to Lender within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter;
[1](b) a net worth of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000.00); and
[1](c) liquid assets (defined as cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities and unencumbered deposits held at federally insured depository institutions) of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000.00).
[P]Compliance with clauses (b) and (c) shall be tested annually based on the financial statements and certifications delivered under Section 6.6. If the DSCR for any calendar quarter is less than 1.25 to 1.00, Borrower shall deliver to Lender, together with its compliance certificate, a written plan detailing the actions Borrower proposes to take to restore compliance, and the failure of the DSCR to equal or exceed 1.25 to 1.00 for two (2) consecutive calendar quarters shall constitute an Event of Default as provided in Article XII.
[H]**6.6 Financial Reporting.** Deliver to Lender: (a) annual audited financial statements of Borrower, prepared in accordance with GAAP by an independent certified public accountant acceptable to Lender, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of Borrower's fiscal year; (b) an annual personal financial statement of Guarantor, in form and detail satisfactory to Lender, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each calendar year; (c) quarterly rent rolls for the Property, certified by Borrower as true, correct and complete, within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter; (d) annual property operating statements for the Property, including a detailed income and expense report and a comparison to budget, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of Borrower's fiscal year; and (e) copies of all Leases and Lease modifications, within ten (10) Business Days after execution as provided in Section 6.4. Each delivery shall be accompanied by a compliance certificate executed by an authorized signatory of Borrower certifying compliance with Section 6.5 and the absence of any Event of Default (or specifying any Event of Default).
[H]**6.7 Single-Purpose Entity Covenants.** Borrower shall at all times maintain its status as a Single-Purpose Entity and shall, without limiting the generality of the foregoing: (a) engage in no business or activity other than the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing, management and disposition of the Property and activities incidental thereto; (b) maintain its own separate books of account, financial records, stationery, invoices, checks and bank accounts, separate and apart from those of any other Person; (c) not commingle its funds or assets with those of any affiliate, member, manager or other Person; (d) hold itself out to the public as a legal entity separate and distinct from any other Person, including its members and affiliates, and conduct its business in its own name; (e) maintain adequate capitalization in light of its contemplated business operations, transactions and liabilities; (f) pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own assets; (g) not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any affiliate, other than customary non-recourse carve-out guaranties in favor of Lender; (h) maintain arm's-length relationships with its affiliates and enter into no transaction with an affiliate except on commercially reasonable terms; (i) not incur any additional indebtedness, secured or unsecured, without Lender's prior written consent; (j) observe all customary formalities regarding its existence, including the maintenance of minutes and written consents; and (k) not hold itself out as being liable for the debts of any affiliate or as a division or part of any other Person.
[H]**6.8 Organizational Documents; Further Assurances.** Prior to or concurrently with the Closing, deliver to Lender an executed Operating Agreement Amendment, executed by all of Borrower's members (Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC), in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Lender, which amends Borrower's Amended and Restated Operating Agreement to (a) restrict Borrower's purpose to the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing, financing and disposition of the Property and activities incidental thereto; (b) incorporate the separateness covenants described in Section 6.7; (c) require the affirmative written consent of an independent manager or an independent director (whose consent shall also be required for any amendment of such provisions) before Borrower may file or consent to any bankruptcy, insolvency or reorganization petition, dissolve, liquidate, merge, consolidate or wind up its affairs; and (d) require Lender's prior written consent to any dissolution, merger, consolidation or transfer of all or substantially all of the Property. Borrower shall deliver to Lender, concurrently with the Closing, (i) a certificate of good standing of Borrower issued by the South Carolina Secretary of State, (ii) a certificate of incumbency and resolutions of Borrower's members authorizing the Loan, and (iii) if requested, a certificate of authority of Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, as general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP. Borrower shall also deliver to Lender, at the Closing, an ALTA lender's title insurance policy (or a pro forma policy or marked-up commitment) in the amount of $14,750,000.00, together with such endorsements as Lender requires, including, without limitation, zoning, access, survey, comprehensive, contiguity, subdivision, encroachment (ALTA 28.1), and future advance endorsements.
[H]**6.9 Inspection.** Permit Lender and its agents, representatives, appraisers, engineers, inspectors and environmental consultants to enter upon and inspect the Property at reasonable times and upon reasonable prior notice (and without notice following an Event of Default), and to examine and copy Borrower's books and records relating to the Property.
[H]**6.10 Notices.** Deliver to Lender, promptly and in any event within five (5) Business Days after Borrower obtains knowledge thereof, written notice of (a) any Event of Default or any event that with notice or lapse of time would constitute an Event of Default; (b) any litigation, arbitration, governmental investigation or administrative proceeding affecting Borrower, Guarantor or the Property that involves a claim in excess of $100,000.00; (c) any notice of violation, citation, stop-work order or other notice from any governmental authority, including SCDHEC and the City of Charleston; (d) any casualty, Condemnation or threat of Condemnation; (e) any default by any Tenant beyond applicable notice and cure periods, any Tenant bankruptcy or insolvency, or any Tenant's vacating of its premises; and (f) any change in Borrower's name, state of organization, organizational identification number, principal place of business or registered agent.
[H]**6.11 Books and Records.** Maintain complete and accurate books and records in accordance with GAAP at Borrower's principal office in Charleston, South Carolina, and permit Lender to inspect the same in accordance with Section 6.9.
[H]**6.12 Estoppel Certificates.** Within ten (10) Business Days after Lender's written request (but not more frequently than once in any twelve (12) month period, except in connection with a default, a proposed sale or a proposed refinancing), deliver to Lender an estoppel certificate certifying as to the status of the Loan Documents, the outstanding principal balance, the absence of defaults and such other matters as Lender may reasonably request.
[H]**6.13 Renovation.** Diligently perform and complete the Renovation Work in accordance with Article IX, within the Renovation Budget and by the Substantial Completion Deadline.
[H]**6.14 Reserves.** Make all deposits to the reserve and escrow accounts required by Article X when due.
[H]**6.15 Management.** Maintain the Property under competent management reasonably acceptable to Lender, and deliver to Lender a copy of any management agreement (and any amendment or termination thereof) within ten (10) Business Days after execution. Borrower shall not enter into any management agreement providing for fees in excess of four percent (4%) of gross revenues from the Property without Lender's prior written consent.
[H]**6.16 Compliance Certificates.** Deliver to Lender, within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter, a certificate of an authorized signatory of Borrower certifying compliance with Sections 6.5, 6.7 and Article VIII and identifying any matter that would constitute a breach thereof.
EOF

Borrower acknowledges that Borrower's Operating Agreement does not restrict indirect or upstream transfers or changes of control, and agrees that this Section 7.3 operates independently of, and is not limited by, the transfer restrictions in its Operating Agreement.
[H]**7.4 Amendment of Organizational Documents.** Amend, modify, restate, terminate or waive any provision of Borrower's Articles of Organization or Operating Agreement, including any SPE provision, separateness covenant, independent manager provision, purpose clause or bankruptcy-remote provision, or take any action to cause Borrower to fail to qualify as a Single-Purpose Entity.
[H]**7.5 Dissolution; Merger; Bankruptcy.** Dissolve, liquidate, wind up, merge, consolidate, convert or divide, or file or consent to the filing of any petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any state insolvency proceeding, or make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or consent to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, without in each case Lender's prior written consent and, where required by its Operating Agreement as amended by the Operating Agreement Amendment, the prior written consent of Borrower's independent manager.
[H]**7.6 Change in Use.** Change the use of the Property from mixed-use retail and office, or use, or permit the use of, the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1, 520 King Street) for residential purposes or for any use prohibited by the land use restriction described in Article VIII.
[H]**7.7 Removal of Fixtures.** Remove, demolish or alter any material fixture, building system or item of personal property affixed to or used in the operation of the Property, except in the ordinary course of maintenance and repair and only if replaced with an item of equal or greater value and utility that is free of liens and subject to Lender's lien.
[H]**7.8 Liens; Partition.** Create or permit any lien on the Property other than the Permitted Exceptions (except for liens for Impositions not yet delinquent and mechanics' liens arising in the ordinary course of the Renovation Work that are bonded over or discharged within thirty (30) days), or institute or permit any partition of the Property or any interest therein.
[H]**7.9 Release or Modification of Leases.** Terminate, accept a surrender of, or consent to the assignment of, any Lease for premises in excess of five thousand (5,000) square feet; release any Tenant or guarantor of a Lease; reduce rent; or grant any material concession, free rent, tenant improvement allowance or leasing commission outside the Renovation Budget or the Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve, without Lender's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.
[H]**7.10 Affiliate Transactions; Commingling.** Enter into any transaction with any affiliate of Borrower except on arm's-length terms disclosed to Lender, make any distribution to its members that would cause a breach of Section 6.5, or commingle its funds with those of any affiliate.
[H]**7.11 Assumption of Debt; Guaranties.** Assume, guarantee or become surety for the obligations of any Person, other than endorsements for collection in the ordinary course and the Guaranty Agreement and Environmental Indemnity Agreement.
[A]ARTICLE VIII
[A]ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND THE SCDHEC LAND USE RESTRICTION
[H]**8.1 Environmental Compliance.** Borrower shall comply, and cause the Property and all Tenants, contractors and agents to comply, with all applicable environmental laws, and shall not cause or permit any Hazardous Substances to be brought upon, stored, used, generated, released or disposed of at, on, under or from the Property, except customary cleaning supplies and de minimis quantities of materials used in the ordinary course of the operation of the Property in compliance with applicable law. Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of any release, threatened release, notice of violation or inquiry from any governmental authority, and shall deliver to Lender copies of all correspondence with SCDHEC relating to the Property or to SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772.
[H]**8.2 The Land Use Restriction.** Borrower acknowledges that the Property is subject to that certain land use restriction and institutional control recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89, RMC Office (the "**Land Use Restriction**"), imposed by SCDHEC in connection with its "No Further Action" determination dated August 12, 2021, for SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772, relating to contamination originating at the adjacent property located at 518 King Street. The Land Use Restriction runs with the land, is binding on Borrower and all Tenants, successors and assigns, and, as it applies to the Property, (a) prohibits the use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Tax Map No. 460-12-04-007, comprising Bay 1 at 520 King Street, approximately 3,800 square feet) for residential purposes, and (b) requires the owner of the Property to maintain, in good condition and working order, the vapor barrier system installed beneath the concrete floor slab of the ground-floor commercial space on Lot 7, and to permit periodic inspection thereof. Borrower shall include in each Lease of the ground floor of Lot 7 an express covenant by the Tenant to comply with the Land Use Restriction and prohibiting residential use.
[H]**8.5 SCDHEC Coordination; Renovation Work.** Before performing any Renovation Work that may affect the floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7, and before performing any work that requires notification to or approval from SCDHEC under the Land Use Restriction, Borrower shall (a) notify SCDHEC in writing and obtain any required approval, (b) notify Lender in writing at least fifteen (15) days in advance, and (c) deliver to Lender copies of all correspondence, approvals and inspection reports relating thereto. Borrower shall cause the Renovation Work (including, without limitation, the HVAC replacement, elevator modernization and façade restoration) to be designed, sequenced and performed so as not to compromise the vapor barrier beneath the Bay 1 slab.
[H]**8.6 No Modification or Termination.** Borrower shall not, without Lender's prior written consent, (a) request, consent to or accept any modification, amendment, termination or release of the Land Use Restriction or of any institutional control, (b) take any action that would cause SCDHEC to reopen SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772 or revoke or modify its "No Further Action" determination, or (c) fail to maintain any institutional control required by SCDHEC.
[H]**8.7 Reporting and Certification.** Borrower shall deliver to Lender (a) within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar year, an officer's certificate certifying compliance with this Article VIII for the preceding year, (b) promptly upon receipt, copies of all inspection reports relating to the vapor barrier and all correspondence with SCDHEC, and (c) promptly upon Lender's request, such other information relating to the environmental condition of the Property as Lender may reasonably require.
[H]**8.8 Environmental Default.** Any failure by Borrower to comply with the Land Use Restriction, the institutional controls described in this Article VIII, or any other provision of this Article VIII, and any modification, termination or release of the Land Use Restriction without Lender's prior written consent, shall constitute an immediate Event of Default without notice or opportunity to cure, and shall constitute a "carve-out event" giving rise to recourse liability under Section 14.15 to the extent provided therein and under the Guaranty Agreement. Borrower acknowledges that Lender has relied on the existence and continued effectiveness of the SCDHEC institutional controls in making the Loan.
[H]**8.9 Environmental Indemnity.** The obligations of Borrower under this Article VIII are in addition to, and not in limitation of, the Environmental Indemnity Agreement, which shall be enforceable in accordance with its terms and shall survive repayment of the Loan, foreclosure, delivery of a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and the release or satisfaction of this Mortgage.

[H]**9.8 Inspections; Fees.** Lender and its inspecting architect or engineer may inspect the Renovation Work at reasonable times and from time to time. Borrower shall pay all reasonable costs of such inspections, including any reinspection fee imposed as a result of work not conforming to the approved plans and specifications or not being ready for inspection.
