If Substantial Completion has not been achieved by such date, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 12.1(i) without any notice or cure period, and Lender shall have no obligation to make any further Advances of the Renovation Holdback. Borrower shall deliver to Lender, within ten (10) Business Days after Substantial Completion, an architect's certificate of substantial completion, the certificate of occupancy, as-built drawings and a final cost statement for the Renovation Work.

Any undisbursed portion of the Renovation Holdback shall not be deemed loaned or committed to Borrower, shall not reduce the Indebtedness, and shall not relieve Borrower of any obligation under this Mortgage. Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may, at its option, apply any undisbursed portion of the Renovation Holdback to the Indebtedness or to the completion of the Renovation Work, in either case without liability to Borrower.
[H]**9.11 Completion Guaranty.** Concurrently with the execution of this Mortgage, Borrower shall cause Guarantor to execute and deliver the Completion Guaranty, unconditionally guaranteeing the completion of the Renovation Work within the Renovation Budget and by the Substantial Completion Deadline. Borrower acknowledges that the completion obligation is a separate obligation of Borrower and Guarantor and that Lender's disbursement of the Renovation Holdback is not a waiver of either obligation.
[H]**9.12 Construction Contract Assignment and Consent.** Borrower shall deliver to Lender, at or prior to Closing, (a) a collateral assignment of the Construction Contract in favor of Lender, and (b) the written consent of Beaufort Builders Group LLC to such collateral assignment (or evidence satisfactory to Lender that no such consent is required). Borrower shall cause the Construction Contract to name Lender as an additional insured and loss payee as its interests appear, and shall not amend, terminate or replace the Construction Contract, or engage any replacement general contractor, without Lender's prior written consent.

[H]**10.2 Capital Replacement Reserve.** Borrower shall deposit with Lender, on the first day of each calendar month, the sum of Six Hundred Forty-Five Dollars and Eighty-Three Cents ($645.83), being the product of $0.25 per square foot per year multiplied by 31,000 square feet of gross building area ($7,750.00 per year) divided by twelve (12) months. Best rating of not less than A-:VII, (b) contain a provision requiring not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Lender of cancellation, non-renewal or material modification (and ten (10) days' notice for non-payment of premium), (c) contain a waiver of subrogation in favor of Lender to the extent permitted by law, (d) be written with deductibles and self-insured retentions reasonably acceptable to Lender, and (e) be primary with respect to any insurance maintained by Lender.
[H]**11.7 Evidence; Renewal.** Borrower shall deliver to Lender, prior to the Closing Date and thereafter not less than ten (10) days before the expiration of each policy, certificates of insurance, or certified copies of policies where required by Lender, naming Lender as mortgagee, loss payee and/or additional insured as applicable, together with evidence of payment of premiums. Borrower shall not cancel, reduce or materially modify any required coverage without Lender's prior written consent.
[H]**11.8 Casualty.** Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of any damage to the Property. Lender, in its reasonable discretion, may elect either (a) to apply the insurance proceeds to the Indebtedness in accordance with Section 13.8, or (b) to permit Borrower to restore the Improvements, provided that (i) no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, (ii) in Lender's reasonable judgment the restoration is economically feasible and can be completed within the earlier of twelve (12) months or the Substantial Completion Deadline, (iii) the proceeds, together with any additional funds deposited by Borrower, are sufficient to complete the restoration, (iv) Borrower demonstrates to Lender's reasonable satisfaction that the Property will generate sufficient income upon restoration to satisfy the covenants in Section 6.5, and (v) the conditions to disbursement set forth in Section 14.13 are satisfied as to the restoration. Any proceeds applied to the Indebtedness under this Section shall be applied at par, without prepayment premium, in accordance with Section 4.8. Borrower shall pay all costs of restoration in excess of available proceeds.
[H]**11.9 Condemnation.** Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of any actual or threatened Condemnation. Lender may participate in any proceeding and Borrower shall not settle or compromise any Condemnation claim without Lender's prior written consent. Any award or payment shall be paid to Lender and applied in accordance with Sections 4.8 and 13.8, or, at Lender's election, released to Borrower for restoration of the remainder of the Property on the conditions set forth in Section 11.8. Borrower irrevocably assigns to Lender all of its right, title and interest in and to any such award, and appoints Lender as its attorney-in-fact to collect and receipt for the same.
[H]**11.10 Failure to Insure.** If Borrower fails to maintain any insurance required by this Article XI, Lender may (but shall not be obligated to) obtain such insurance and pay the premium therefor, and any amount so paid shall be an additional advance secured by this Mortgage, shall bear interest at the Default Rate, and shall be repayable on demand. Such failure shall constitute an Event of Default.

[H]**9.4 Conditions to Each Advance.** Lender's obligation to make any Advance of the Renovation Holdback is subject to the satisfaction of each of the following conditions: (a) no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, and no event has occurred that with notice or lapse of time would constitute an Event of Default; (b) the representations and warranties in Article V are true and correct in all material respects; (c) Borrower has delivered a complete draw request in accordance with Section 9.3; (d) the requested amount does not exceed the available allocation for the applicable budget line item or the remaining Renovation Holdback; (e) Borrower has funded, or concurrently funds, its proportionate share of the equity allocable to the work covered by the draw request in accordance with **Exhibit C**, and has delivered evidence thereof; (f) all work covered by prior draws has been completed and paid for and all unconditional lien waivers for such work have been delivered; (g) no mechanic's or materialmen's lien has been filed against the Property that has not been bonded over or discharged of record; (h) the Renovation Work is on schedule to achieve Substantial Completion by the Substantial Completion Deadline; and (i) Borrower has paid all costs, fees and expenses of Lender's inspector and title insurer incurred in connection with the draw.
[H]**9.5 Retainage.** Lender shall retain ten percent (10%) of each disbursement from the Renovation Holdback (the "**Retainage**") until Substantial Completion of the Renovation Work has been achieved in accordance with Section 9.9.
[H]**9.6 Release of Retainage.** Lender shall release the Retainage upon Lender's receipt of (a) satisfactory evidence of Substantial Completion, including the architect's certification and the certificate of occupancy, (b) final unconditional lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors and suppliers, (c) a final title date-down endorsement confirming no intervening liens, (d) a certification that the Renovation Work has been completed within the Renovation Budget and that all costs of the Renovation Work have been paid in full, and (e) evidence of the continued effectiveness of all insurance required by Article XI, including the transition from builder's risk coverage to permanent property coverage.
[H]**9.7 Cost Overruns; Borrower Equity.** Borrower shall be responsible for all costs of the Renovation Work in excess of the Renovation Holdback, including the $600,000.00 by which the $2,850,000.00 contract sum under the Construction Contract exceeds the Renovation Holdback and the $300,000.00 of soft costs and contingency outside the Construction Contract. Borrower shall fund such amounts from its own funds as and when required by the progress of the Renovation Work, and shall, within ten (10) days after Lender's written demand, deposit with Lender any amount necessary to cure any deficiency in the Renovation Budget or to complete the Renovation Work.
[H]**9.8 Inspections; Fees.** Lender and its inspecting architect or engineer may inspect the Renovation Work at reasonable times and from time to time. Borrower shall pay all reasonable costs of such inspections, including any reinspection fee imposed as a result of work not conforming to the approved plans and specifications or not being ready for inspection.
[H]**9.9 Substantial Completion.** Borrower shall achieve Substantial Completion of the Renovation Work on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline of June 15, 2026. If Substantial Completion has not been achieved by such date, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 12.1(i) without any notice or cure period, and Lender shall have no obligation to make any further Advances of the Renovation Holdback. Borrower shall deliver to Lender, within ten (10) Business Days after Substantial Completion, an architect's certificate of substantial completion, the certificate of occupancy, as-built drawings and a final cost statement for the Renovation Work.
[H]**9.10 No Commitment Beyond Holdback; Effect of Default.** Lender shall have no obligation to disburse any portion of the Renovation Holdback if an Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, and Lender may suspend disbursements upon the occurrence of any event that, with notice or lapse of time, would constitute an Event of Default. Any undisbursed portion of the Renovation Holdback shall not be deemed loaned or committed to Borrower, shall not reduce the Indebtedness, and shall not relieve Borrower of any obligation under this Mortgage. Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may, at its option, apply any undisbursed portion of the Renovation Holdback to the Indebtedness or to the completion of the Renovation Work, in either case without liability to Borrower.
[H]**9.11 Completion Guaranty.** Concurrently with the execution of this Mortgage, Borrower shall cause Guarantor to execute and deliver the Completion Guaranty, unconditionally guaranteeing the completion of the Renovation Work within the Renovation Budget and by the Substantial Completion Deadline. The Completion Guaranty shall be a Loan Document, and any default thereunder shall constitute an Event of Default under this Mortgage. Borrower acknowledges that the completion obligation is a separate obligation of Borrower and Guarantor and that Lender's disbursement of the Renovation Holdback is not a waiver of either obligation.
[H]**9.12 Construction Contract Assignment and Consent.** Borrower shall deliver to Lender, at or prior to Closing, (a) a collateral assignment of the Construction Contract in favor of Lender, and (b) the written consent of Beaufort Builders Group LLC to such collateral assignment (or evidence satisfactory to Lender that no such consent is required). Borrower shall cause the Construction Contract to name Lender as an additional insured and loss payee as its interests appear, and shall not amend, terminate or replace the Construction Contract, or engage any replacement general contractor, without Lender's prior written consent.

[A]RESERVE AND ESCROW ACCOUNTS
[H]**10.1 Tax and Insurance Escrow.** Borrower shall deposit with Lender, on the Closing Date and on the first day of each calendar month thereafter, an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual real property taxes and casualty and liability insurance premiums for the Property, covering all three (3) tax parcels (Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008 and 460-12-04-009). [H]**10.2 Capital Replacement Reserve.** Borrower shall deposit with Lender, on the first day of each calendar month, the sum of Six Hundred Forty-Five Dollars and Eighty-Three Cents ($645.83), being the product of $0.25 per square foot per year multiplied by 31,000 square feet of gross building area ($7,750.00 per year) divided by twelve (12) months. Funds in the capital replacement reserve shall be disbursed to Borrower upon Lender's approval of qualifying capital expenditures, subject to Lender's reasonable review and approval procedures. Disbursements from the reserve shall be subject to Lender's prior written approval and shall be used exclusively for tenant improvement costs and leasing commissions incurred in connection with the leasing of vacant space at the Property, and shall not be used for any cost included in the Renovation Budget except to the extent Lender approves in writing an allocation between the two sources of funds. Borrower hereby grants to Lender a security interest in each such account and all sums held therein, and authorizes Lender to file UCC financing statements and to exercise control over such accounts, including by executing a deposit account control agreement in customary form. Lender shall have no obligation to invest, or to obtain any particular yield on, any funds held in such accounts, and shall not be liable for any loss absent its gross negligence or willful misconduct. [H]**11.1 Property Insurance.** Borrower shall maintain at all times, with insurers acceptable to Lender, comprehensive all-risk ("special form") property insurance covering the Property and all Improvements and betterments on a replacement cost basis, with an agreed amount endorsement (waiver of coinsurance), in an amount not less than the full replacement cost of the Improvements and not less than the outstanding Indebtedness. Coverage shall include, without limitation, fire, windstorm, hail, explosion, vandalism, malicious mischief, water damage, sprinkler leakage, ordinance or law coverage, equipment breakdown and such other perils as Lender may reasonably require, and shall name Lender as mortgagee and loss payee pursuant to a standard mortgagee clause.
[H]**11.2 Commercial General Liability.** Borrower shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with minimum limits of Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000.00) per occurrence and Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000.00) in the aggregate, including premises liability, operations liability, products and completed operations, and personal and advertising injury coverage. [H]**11.3 Flood Insurance.** Borrower shall maintain flood insurance on the Property in an amount not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000.00), with Lender named as mortgagee and loss payee. Borrower acknowledges that the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X, that flood insurance may not be required by federal regulation for property in Zone X, and that Lender nevertheless requires such coverage as a condition of the Loan, and agrees that such requirement is reasonable and is not subject to challenge by Borrower.
[H]**11.4 Builder's Risk.** During the period from the Closing Date through Substantial Completion of the Renovation Work, Borrower shall maintain builder's risk insurance on a completed value basis in an amount not less than the full Renovation Budget of Three Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($3,150,000.00), covering the Property and the Renovation Work against all risks of physical loss or damage during the course of construction, including coverage for materials stored off-site, soft costs, and the increased cost of construction due to applicable building code changes. Lender shall be named as mortgagee and loss payee on such policy.
[H]**11.5 Other Insurance.** Borrower shall maintain (a) workers' compensation insurance in the amounts required by the laws of the State of South Carolina, covering all employees of Borrower and, to the extent not covered under the general contractor's policies, all persons engaged in the Renovation Work; (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance in an amount not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000.00), providing excess coverage over the commercial general liability, automobile liability and employers' liability policies; and (c) such other insurance coverages as Lender may reasonably require from time to time, in such amounts and with such carriers as are acceptable to Lender.
[H]**11.6 Policy Requirements.** All insurance policies required by this Article XI shall (a) be issued by insurers licensed to do business in the State of South Carolina having an A.M. Best rating of not less than A-:VII, (b) contain a provision requiring not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Lender of cancellation, non-renewal or material modification (and ten (10) days' notice for non-payment of premium), (c) contain a waiver of subrogation in favor of Lender to the extent permitted by law, (d) be written with deductibles and self-insured retentions reasonably acceptable to Lender, and (e) be primary with respect to any insurance maintained by Lender.
[H]**11.7 Evidence; Renewal.** Borrower shall deliver to Lender, prior to the Closing Date and thereafter not less than ten (10) days before the expiration of each policy, certificates of insurance, or certified copies of policies where required by Lender, naming Lender as mortgagee, loss payee and/or additional insured as applicable, together with evidence of payment of premiums. Borrower shall not cancel, reduce or materially modify any required coverage without Lender's prior written consent.
[H]**11.8 Casualty.** Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of any damage to the Property. Lender, in its reasonable discretion, may elect either (a) to apply the insurance proceeds to the Indebtedness in accordance with Section 13.8, or (b) to permit Borrower to restore the Improvements, provided that (i) no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, (ii) in Lender's reasonable judgment the restoration is economically feasible and can be completed within the earlier of twelve (12) months or the Substantial Completion Deadline, (iii) the proceeds, together with any additional funds deposited by Borrower, are sufficient to complete the restoration, (iv) Borrower demonstrates to Lender's reasonable satisfaction that the Property will generate sufficient income upon restoration to satisfy the covenants in Section 6.5, and (v) the conditions to disbursement set forth in Section 14.13 are satisfied as to the restoration. Any proceeds applied to the Indebtedness under this Section shall be applied at par, without prepayment premium, in accordance with Section 4.8. Borrower shall pay all costs of restoration in excess of available proceeds.

Lender may participate in any proceeding and Borrower shall not settle or compromise any Condemnation claim without Lender's prior written consent. [A]ARTICLE XII
[A]EVENTS OF DEFAULT
[H]**12.1 Events of Default.** Each of the following shall constitute an Event of Default under this Mortgage:
[1](a) Borrower's failure to pay any installment of principal, interest or any other amount due under the Loan Documents on or before the date on which it is due, subject to the cure period in Section 12.2(a);
[1](b) Borrower's breach of any covenant, agreement or obligation contained in the Loan Documents, continuing beyond the applicable cure period in Section 12.2;
[1](c) any representation or warranty made by Borrower or Guarantor in connection with the Loan or in any Loan Document proving to be materially false, misleading or inaccurate in any material respect when made or deemed made;
[1](d) the filing of a petition in bankruptcy by or against Borrower or Guarantor, the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian for any substantial part of the property or assets of Borrower or Guarantor, any assignment for the benefit of creditors by Borrower or Guarantor, or the commencement of any similar insolvency proceeding;
[1](e) a default by Borrower or Guarantor under any other indebtedness for borrowed money in an amount exceeding Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($250,000.00), individually or in the aggregate, which default is not cured within any applicable cure or grace period;
[1](f) Borrower's failure to maintain any insurance required under Article XI;
[1](g) any violation of the transfer restrictions set forth in Sections 7.2 or 7.3;
[1](h) any breach of the Single-Purpose Entity covenants set forth in Section 6.7, or any failure to maintain the organizational provisions required by Section 6.8;
[1](i) failure by Borrower to achieve Substantial Completion of the Renovation Work by the Substantial Completion Deadline of June 15, 2026;
[1](j) the DSCR falling below 1.25 to 1.00 for two (2) consecutive calendar quarters following the commencement of DSCR testing under Section 6.5(a);
[1](k) any failure to comply with, or any modification, termination, release or violation of, the Land Use Restriction or the institutional controls described in Article VIII;
[1](l) any failure by Borrower to fund its equity contributions to the Renovation Work as required by Section 9.7, or any failure by Borrower to fund any reserve or escrow deposit required by Article X within ten (10) days after the date due;
[1](m) any default by Borrower or Guarantor under the Guaranty Agreement, the Completion Guaranty, the Environmental Indemnity Agreement or any other Loan Document;
[1](n) a material adverse change in the financial condition, business, assets or operations of Borrower or Guarantor that, in Lender's reasonable judgment, materially impairs the ability of Borrower or Guarantor to perform its obligations under the Loan Documents;
[1](o) the attachment, sequestration, levy or execution against the Property or any material portion thereof that is not released of record within thirty (30) days; or
[1](p) the occurrence of any other event or condition that constitutes an Event of Default as defined in any other Loan Document.
[H]**12.2 Cure Periods.** The following cure periods shall apply to the Events of Default described in Section 12.1:
[1](a) **Payment Defaults.** Five (5) Business Days from the date on which payment was due. The assessment of a late charge under Section 4.10 shall not extend this cure period.
[1](b) **Non-Monetary Defaults** (other than the defaults described in Section 12.3). Thirty (30) calendar days after written notice from Lender to Borrower of such default; provided, however, that if the default is of a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) calendar days and Borrower has commenced and is diligently pursuing the cure thereof, the cure period shall be extended for an additional period not to exceed sixty (60) calendar days (for a total cure period not to exceed ninety (90) calendar days).
[H]**12.3 Defaults Without Cure.** Any breach of the Single-Purpose Entity covenants set forth in Section 6.7, the transfer restrictions set forth in Sections 7.2 or 7.3, or the provisions of Article VIII, shall constitute an immediate Event of Default without notice or opportunity to cure. Any Event of Default described in Section 12.1(d), (c), (f) or (i) shall likewise not be subject to a cure period.
[H]**12.4 Notice.** Lender shall not be required to give notice of any Event of Default except where this Mortgage expressly so provides, and any notice given as a condition to acceleration or the exercise of any remedy shall be deemed given in accordance with Section 14.4.
[H]**12.5 Remedies Cumulative.** No right or remedy of Lender is exclusive of any other right or remedy, and no delay or omission by Lender in exercising any right or remedy shall impair it or constitute a waiver thereof. The exercise of any one right or remedy shall not preclude the exercise of any other, and Lender may exercise its rights and remedies concurrently, cumulatively and in any order.
[A]ARTICLE XIII
[A]REMEDIES
[H]**13.1 Remedies Upon Default.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may, at its option and in addition to all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity: (a) declare the entire Indebtedness immediately due and payable, whereupon it shall become immediately due and payable without further notice, presentment, demand, protest or notice of any kind, all of which Borrower waives; (b) apply the Default Rate; (c) enforce the absolute assignment of rents in Article III; (d) foreclose this Mortgage in accordance with Section 13.2; (e) seek the appointment of a receiver in accordance with Section 13.3; (f) exercise its rights and remedies as a secured party under the UCC in accordance with Section 13.5; (g) take possession of the Property and collect the rents and profits thereof; (h) cure the default on Borrower's behalf in accordance with Section 13.9; (i) suspend disbursement of the Renovation Holdback; and (j) exercise any other right or remedy available under the Loan Documents or applicable law.
[H]**13.2 Judicial Foreclosure.** Lender may foreclose this Mortgage by an action in the Court of Common Pleas for Charleston County, South Carolina (or in any other court of competent jurisdiction), in accordance with the laws of the State of South Carolina. Borrower acknowledges that South Carolina is a judicial foreclosure state, that this Mortgage does not and shall not confer any power of sale, and that Lender's only remedy by way of foreclosure of the lien of this Mortgage is by judicial action. Lender may, in any such action, seek a judgment for the Indebtedness, a decree of foreclosure and sale of the Property, the appointment of a receiver, and, to the extent permitted by law, a deficiency judgment against Borrower as provided in Section 13.7. Lender may bid at any foreclosure sale.
[H]**13.3 Receivership.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender shall be entitled, as a matter of right and without notice (to the extent permitted by law) and without regard to the adequacy of its security or the solvency of Borrower, to the appointment of a receiver of the Property and of the rents, issues and profits thereof, in any judicial proceeding to enforce this Mortgage or in any separate proceeding. Borrower irrevocably consents to such appointment and waives any objection thereto. The receiver shall have all powers customarily granted to receivers of commercial real property, including the power to lease, manage, operate, repair and maintain the Property, to collect rents and to make disbursements. Any receiver appointed shall be Lender's nominee unless the court otherwise orders, and the receiver's fees and expenses shall be borne by Borrower.
[H]**13.4 Enforcement of Assignment of Rents.** Without limiting Article III, upon an Event of Default Lender may, without any court order, appointment of a receiver or further consent of Borrower, notify Tenants to pay rents directly to Lender, collect and apply such rents, and exercise all rights of Borrower as landlord under the Leases, subject to the Assignment of Rents Act. Lender may also, in its discretion, seek the appointment of a receiver under Section 13.3 in lieu of or in addition to direct collection.
[H]**13.5 Security Agreement Remedies.** Lender may exercise all rights and remedies of a secured party under the UCC, including the right to take possession of the personal property and fixtures collateral, to require Borrower to assemble the collateral and make it available to Lender at a convenient place, and to sell, lease or otherwise dispose of the collateral at public or private sale upon such notice as is required by the UCC. Borrower agrees that ten (10) days' written notice of any public or private sale constitutes reasonable notification. Any sale may be conducted as a unit or in parcels, and Lender may be the purchaser at any sale.
[H]**13.6 Possession; Entry.** Lender may enter upon and take possession of the Property in any lawful manner, exclude Borrower and its agents, and use, operate, manage and lease the Property. Borrower shall, upon demand, deliver possession of the Property and all books, records, keys and security deposits relating thereto.
[H]**13.7 Deficiency.** In the event the proceeds of any foreclosure sale or other disposition of the Property are insufficient to pay the Indebtedness in full, Borrower shall be liable for the deficiency, to the extent provided in Section 14.15 and applicable law, and Lender may seek a deficiency judgment in accordance with South Carolina law.
[H]**13.8 Application of Proceeds.** The proceeds of any foreclosure sale, UCC sale or other realization on the Property, and any insurance proceeds or Condemnation awards applied to the Indebtedness, shall be applied in the order set forth in Section 4.9, and any surplus shall be paid to Borrower or to such other Person as may be entitled thereto by law.
[H]**13.9 Lender's Right to Cure.** If Borrower fails to perform any covenant or obligation under this Mortgage, Lender may (but shall not be obligated to) perform it on Borrower's behalf, including by paying Impositions, insurance premiums, mechanics' liens, repair costs, or costs of completing the Renovation Work. Any amount so expended shall be an additional advance secured by this Mortgage, shall bear interest at the Default Rate from the date of expenditure, and shall be repayable on demand. Lender shall give Borrower notice of any such expenditure promptly after making it, but the giving of notice shall not be a condition to the effectiveness of the advance.
[H]**13.10 Expenses as Additional Indebtedness.** All costs and expenses incurred by Lender in connection with the enforcement of the Loan Documents, including reasonable attorneys' fees, court costs, expert and consultant fees, title charges, and the costs of any inspection, appraisal or environmental assessment obtained following an Event of Default, shall be additional Indebtedness secured by this Mortgage and repayable on demand.
[H]**13.11 No Waiver; No Release.** No forbearance by Lender, no acceptance of a partial payment, and no extension of time shall constitute a waiver of any Event of Default or of any right or remedy, or a release of Borrower or Guarantor, unless expressly set forth in a writing signed by Lender. No acceptance of any payment after the occurrence of an Event of Default shall cure such Event of Default or reinstate the Loan unless Lender so agrees in writing.
[H]**13.12 Absolute Obligations.** Borrower's obligations under this Mortgage are absolute and unconditional and are not subject to any defense, setoff, counterclaim or recoupment arising out of any claim Borrower may have against Lender, any Tenant, any contractor or any other Person, all of which Borrower waives to the fullest extent permitted by law. Borrower's obligation to pay and perform is independent of the performance of any obligation of any other Person, including any Tenant or Guarantor.
[A]ARTICLE XIV
[A]MISCELLANEOUS
[H]**14.1 Governing Law.** This Mortgage shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of South Carolina, without regard to principles of conflicts of law that would require the application of the laws of another jurisdiction.
[H]**14.2 Jurisdiction and Venue.** Borrower irrevocably submits to the jurisdiction of the courts of the State of South Carolina and of the United States District Court for the District of South Carolina for purposes of any action arising out of or relating to this Mortgage, agrees that venue in Charleston County, South Carolina, is proper, and waives any objection based on forum non conveniens. Nothing in this Section shall limit Lender's right to bring an action in any other court of competent jurisdiction to enforce this Mortgage or to realize on its collateral, including in any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding.
[H]**14.3 Waiver of Jury Trial.** TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, BORROWER AND LENDER EACH KNOWINGLY, VOLUNTARILY AND INTENTIONALLY WAIVE ANY RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS MORTGAGE, THE NOTE, THE OTHER LOAN DOCUMENTS OR THE LOAN. THIS WAIVER IS A MATERIAL INDUCEMENT TO LENDER'S MAKING OF THE LOAN.
[H]**14.4 Notices.** All notices, demands, consents and other communications shall be in writing and shall be deemed given (a) when delivered personally, (b) one (1) Business Day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, (c) three (3) Business Days after deposit in the United States mail, certified or registered, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, or (d) when sent by electronic mail, provided that a copy is also delivered by one of the foregoing methods, in each case addressed as follows (or to such other address as a party designates by notice):
[1]**If to Lender:** Calverley Heritage Bank, 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, Georgia 31401, Attention: Marcus Prideaux, Senior Vice President — Commercial Real Estate Lending, Email: mprideaux@coastalheritagebank.com; with a copy to Fielding, Ashworth & Cole LLP, Charleston, South Carolina, Attention: Catherine Ashworth, Partner.
[1]**If to Borrower:** Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401, Attention: Neil Ashford Graydon, Managing Member; with a copy to Cartwright & Lyons LLP, Charleston, South Carolina.
[1]**If to Guarantor:** Neil Ashford Graydon, 14 Church Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29401.
[H]**14.5 No Oral Modification.** This Mortgage may not be amended, modified, supplemented or waived except by a written instrument signed by Borrower and Lender (and, where its rights are affected, Guarantor), and no waiver shall extend to any subsequent or other default.
[H]**14.6 Severability.** If any provision of this Mortgage is held to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable, such provision shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law and the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.
[H]**14.7 Entire Agreement; Relationship to Other Loan Documents.** The Loan Documents constitute the entire agreement between Borrower and Lender with respect to the Loan and supersede all prior agreements and understandings, including the Term Sheet dated April 1, 2025. In the event of any conflict between this Mortgage and the Note, the Note shall control as to the payment terms, and this Mortgage shall control as to the collateral, remedies and covenants. In the event of any conflict between this Mortgage and any other Loan Document, the Loan Document imposing the higher standard on Borrower or the greater protection to Lender shall control, except that the Note shall control as to the interest rate, payment terms and prepayment provisions.
[H]**14.8 Successors and Assigns.** This Mortgage shall inure to the benefit of Lender, its successors and assigns (including any assignee or participant of the Loan), and shall be binding upon Borrower, its successors and permitted assigns. Borrower may not assign any of its rights hereunder without Lender's prior written consent. Lender may assign or participate the Loan and this Mortgage without Borrower's consent, and may disclose information concerning Borrower and the Property to any actual or prospective assignee, participant, servicer or rating agency, subject to customary confidentiality obligations.
[H]**14.9 Expenses and Indemnity.** Borrower shall pay all out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred by Lender in connection with the origination, underwriting, documentation, closing, administration, enforcement and preservation of the Loan and this Mortgage, including reasonable attorneys' fees and disbursements, appraisal fees, environmental report fees, title insurance premiums, survey costs, recording fees, documentary stamp taxes, UCC filing and search fees, and construction inspection fees. Borrower shall indemnify, defend and hold Lender harmless from and against all claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to (a) the Property, including any environmental condition or any violation of the Land Use Restriction, (b) the ownership, operation, renovation or leasing of the Property, (c) any Lease or any claim of any Tenant, (d) any breach by Borrower of any representation, warranty or covenant in the Loan Documents, and (e) any claim of any contractor, subcontractor, supplier or other Person arising from the Renovation Work, except to the extent caused by Lender's gross negligence or willful misconduct. [CSM]PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION
[GAP]
[TITLE]DRAFTING ISSUES MEMORANDUM
[SUBTITLE]Mortgage and Security Agreement — Calverley Heritage Bank / Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC
[C]CHB CRE Loan No. 2025-CHS-0047 — 520–534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403
[C]Principal Amount $14,750,000.00
[GAP]
[T]
[R]TO | Catherine "Kit" Ashworth, Partner, Real Estate Practice Group Chair
[R]FROM | Jordan Vickers, Associate
[R]CC | File
[R]DATE | March 28, 2025
[R]RE | Issues on first draft of Mortgage and Security Agreement; items requiring instruction before delivery to Lender
[GAP]
[P]This memorandum accompanies the first draft of the Mortgage and Security Agreement (the "**Mortgage**") for the above-referenced loan (the "**Loan**") and records the issues identified in preparing it. It follows your markup notes dated March 18, 2025 and addresses each item you asked me to prioritize — the restructuring of the assignment of rents from a collateral to an absolute assignment, the single-purpose entity and operating agreement problem (including the form of operating agreement amendment), and the yield maintenance formula — together with a number of discrepancies in the source record that I do not believe can be resolved by drafting alone.
[A]I. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND SOURCES REVIEWED
[P]I have read each document in the loan file in full and have independently recomputed every figure used in the Mortgage rather than adopting any figure as quoted. The sources I relied on, and the weight I have given each, are as follows:
[T]
[R]Source | Date | Use in the draft | Reliance
[R]Executed Term Sheet, CHB CRE Loan No. 2025-CHS-0047 | April 1, 2025 | Governing commercial terms; every economic and covenant term in the Mortgage is drawn from it | Primary — controlling where inconsistent with any other source
[R]Title Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178 (Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC / Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc.) | Effective February 28, 2025 | Legal description (Exhibit A), Permitted Exceptions (Exhibit B), closing conditions | Primary for title
[R]Phase I ESA, Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC, Report No. CLR-2025-0119 | January 28, 2025 | CREC on Lot 7, SCDHEC Land Use Restriction, vapor barrier and institutional-control covenants (Article VIII) | Primary for environmental
[R]Appraisal, Pinnacle Valuation Services LLC, File PVS-2025-0214-CHS | February 14, 2025 | Values, NOI, occupancy, lease commentary | Secondary — figures re-verified
[R]Rent Roll and Lease Abstracts (workbook) | Current as of drafting | Exhibit D; lease provisions; occupancy | Secondary — figures re-verified; several internal errors identified
[R]Renovation Budget and Draw Schedule (workbook) | Current as of drafting | Exhibit C; disbursement mechanics in Article IX | Secondary — arithmetic errors identified
[R]Redacted Summary of Amended and Restated Operating Agreement (Cartwright & Lyons LLP) | Amended through March 1, 2025 | Authority, SPE status, transfer restrictions, reporting | Secondary and incomplete — summary only; full agreement required
[R]Your markup notes | March 18, 2025 | Drafting instructions | Instruction
[GAP]
[P]Where a source is a summary rather than an original (the operating agreement summary is expressly a redacted summary; the Phase I document is an executive summary extracted from a full report), I have said so in the relevant issue and have not treated the summary as a substitute for the underlying document. The full Phase I report and the full operating agreement should be obtained and reviewed before we express any opinion on the environmental condition of the Property or on Borrower's separateness.
[A]II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — TOP RISK REGISTER
[P]The following are the matters that, in my view, require resolution before the Mortgage is delivered to Marcus Prideaux. Each is cross-referenced to the detailed discussion below. The ranking reflects the consequence to the Bank if the item is not addressed, not the difficulty of the fix.
[T]
[R]Rank | Issue | Consequence if not addressed | Draft treatment | Ref.
[R]1 | The DSCR covenant of 1.25x is not attainable on any income projection in the file, including the stabilized case | A covenant default at the first test date is effectively pre-ordained; the covenant as drafted converts a performing loan into a defaulted loan at month 24–27 | Drafted as instructed; flagged for restructuring | Issues 1–2
[R]2 | Occupancy is misstated as 68% throughout the file; the correct figure is 56.13% | Underwriting, LTV commentary, lease-up assumptions and any occupancy-based covenant or guaranty burn-off rest on a 4,000 SF error | Not recited in the Mortgage; corrected in Exhibit D | Issue 3
[R]3 | Borrower is not a single-purpose, bankruptcy-remote entity, and the required amendment has not been delivered | The non-recourse structure and the recourse carve-outs — the entire basis of the Loan — are unenforceable in substance; also a misrepresentation risk if we draft the representation as instructed | Article VI/6.7–6.8 and Article V/5.7 drafted conditionally on the amendment | Issues 18–19
[R]4 | The Anson Lane strip was conveyed by quitclaim deed only, and the description in the term sheet omits the recorded plat reference | Possible collateral gap on the parcel that provides rear access to all three lots; title coverage may be qualified | Parcel Two described by reference to Plat Book 64 at Page 91; endorsements required | Issue 9
[R]5 | Title is presently vested in Hampstead Village Holdings LLC, not Borrower | If the deed is not recorded immediately before the Mortgage, the Mortgage is executed by a non-owner and the lien fails | Closing sequencing condition and representation in Section 5.3 | Issue 8
[R]6 | The yield maintenance formula in the term sheet is ambiguous on four variables, and your drafting instruction differs from the term sheet's economics | An unenforceable or unadministrable prepayment premium; a court could treat it as a penalty | Drafted to the term sheet's greater-of structure with all four variables defined; flagged for confirmation | Issue 4
[R]7 | Estoppels and SNDAs are conditions precedent, but the Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease has no estoppel obligation, no SNDA provision and no assignment clause | The Bank cannot compel delivery; closing may fail on a condition the borrower cannot satisfy without tenant goodwill | Representations, covenant and lease-amendment undertaking in Article III | Issue 21
[R]8 | Sources and uses leave approximately $440,000 of closing costs, the TI/LC reserve and leasing commissions unfunded | Borrower may be unable to close, or may fund the gap by borrowing — which the negative covenants prohibit | Reserve and expense obligations drafted; gap flagged | Issue 13
[R]9 | The SCDHEC land use restriction on Lot 7 is a permanent, non-removable title matter with continuing affirmative obligations | An uncured breach can reopen the site file and impair both value and the Bank's collateral; the recourse carve-out for environmental liability is currently drafted to include pre-existing conditions | Article VIII drafted as specific covenants with an immediate default; recourse scope flagged | Issues 24–26
[R]10 | The Guaranty is described as "full recourse" in its heading but as non-recourse with carve-outs in its operative text, and the interest carry covers only 14 months | The guaranty does not address the DSCR shortfall it was presumably intended to mitigate | Mortgage references the Guaranty neutrally; flagged for the Guaranty drafter | Issue 5
[R]11 | Permitted Exceptions have never been approved by the Bank in writing, and a future advance endorsement is essential given the $2,250,000 holdback | Priority of the holdback advances could be lost to intervening liens | Exhibit B drafted with conditions to approval | Issue 11
[R]12 | Whether the assignment of rents is to be a separate recorded instrument is unresolved in the term sheet itself | A filing/recording gap on the rent collateral; tenant and title insurer objections at closing | Absolute assignment included in Article III, with a separate-instrument undertaking | Issue 6
[GAP]
[P]The remainder of this memorandum discusses these and the other issues in detail, in the order in which they arise in the Mortgage. Section XII lists the matters that the Mortgage deliberately does not address and the reason. Appendix A reconciles every figure. Appendix B maps each issue to its source. Appendix C lists the provisions I have supplied as counsel, which are not in the term sheet and therefore require the Bank's approval.
EOF
wc -w memo.txt"}

[A]III. SUMMARY OF THE DRAFT AND THE STRUCTURAL DECISIONS MADE
[P]The Mortgage is drafted as a Article II granting clause plus an integrated Article III absolute assignment of rents, followed by representations, affirmative and negative covenants, a dedicated renovation and disbursement article, a dedicated environmental article addressing the SCDHEC restriction, default and remedy articles, and five exhibits. The following structural decisions should be noted, because each departs from the firm template or resolves an ambiguity in the record:
[1]**(a) No separate loan agreement is contemplated.** The term sheet lists the Loan Documents in Section 14.3 and does not include a loan agreement. Consequently, every covenant that would ordinarily live in a loan agreement — DSCR, net worth and liquidity, reporting, SPE, transfer restrictions, leasing, reserves — has been drafted into the Mortgage. This makes the Mortgage the principal covenant instrument for the transaction, which is unusual for a loan of this size and puts significant weight on a recorded instrument. If the Bank intends to syndicate or securitize, I recommend converting those provisions to a separate Loan Agreement before closing. I have not done so without instruction.
[1]**(b) The assignment of rents is absolute, not collateral.** Article III is drafted as an unconditional and present assignment, expressly not "as additional security," with a revocable license back to Borrower in Section 3.2 and enforcement on default in Section 3.3 without a court order or receiver. This follows your instruction and the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act. Please note the term sheet itself is permissive: Section 5.2 allows the assignment to be included in the Mortgage or executed separately, while Sections 12.1(a) and 14.3(b)–(c) list an Assignment of Leases and Rents as a document to be executed, and Section 14.3(c) refers to it being recorded "if prepared as a separate instrument." I have followed your preference and Section 5.2, and have added Section 3.8 obliging Borrower to execute a separate instrument on demand. See Issue 6.
[1]**(c) The assignment of rents is in the Mortgage but the UCC collateral is also a fixture filing.** Section 2.3 authorizes both a UCC-1 with the Secretary of State and a fixture filing with the RMC Office, consistent with your note and Requirement 4 of the title commitment.
[1]**(d) No power of sale.** Consistent with your instruction, Section 2.8 states affirmatively that no power of sale is granted and Article XIII forecloses only judicially. I have added an express acknowledgment that South Carolina does not permit power-of-sale foreclosure, which reads oddly in a commercial mortgage but is useful if the Loan is ever assigned to an out-of-state holder.
[1]**(e) The environmental obligations are article-length, not a standard covenant.** Because the title commitment's Special Instruction 1 and the Phase I ESA's recommendation 6(d) both require specific covenants addressing the SCDHEC land use restriction, a vapor barrier maintenance obligation and a default triggered by non-compliance, I have drafted Article VIII as a stand-alone article. A generic environmental compliance clause would not have satisfied either document.
[1]**(f) The representations are drafted to be true when made.** This is the one point on which I have departed from your instruction, and I have set out my reasoning in Issue 18. In short, I do not think we can draft a representation that Borrower's organizational documents contain the required SPE provisions when we know they do not; the representation would be false on its face, would be a misrepresentation to the Bank's credit file, and would itself trigger the fraud carve-out in Section 14.15. I have instead drafted the representation to speak "on and as of the Closing Date, and after giving effect to the Operating Agreement Amendment delivered at Closing," and made delivery of that amendment a condition precedent.
[A]IV. ISSUES REQUIRING INSTRUCTION BEFORE THE DRAFT IS FINALIZED
[H]**Issue 1 — The 1.25x DSCR covenant cannot be satisfied, on any projection in the file.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §§7.1, 11.1(i); Appraisal §6.2–6.3; Rent Roll workbook, "Vacancy Schedule" tab.
[P]This is the single most serious problem in the transaction. The term sheet requires a DSCR of not less than 1.25x, tested quarterly from the first full calendar quarter after month 24, with a default triggered by two consecutive quarters below the covenant. I have computed the DSCR on every income figure in the file, at the note rate of 5.85% (the SOFR floor of 3.00% plus the 285 basis point spread) on $14,750,000:
[T]
[R]NOI basis | NOI | DSCR on amortizing debt service ($1,124,239/yr) | DSCR on interest-only debt service ($862,875/yr)
[R]In-place, per rent roll | $320,100 | 0.28x | 0.37x
[R]As-is, per appraisal (low–high) | $332,000 – $345,000 | 0.30x – 0.31x | 0.38x – 0.40x
[R]Stabilized, per appraisal (low–high) | $582,000 – $592,000 | 0.52x – 0.53x | 0.67x – 0.69x
[R]Stabilized, per rent roll best case | $622,772 | 0.55x | 0.72x
[P]On the stabilized best case, the NOI required to satisfy 1.25x is $1,405,299 on amortizing debt service, or $1,078,594 on interest-only debt service. The projected stabilized NOI is $587,000 at the appraisal's midpoint. Put another way, the largest loan that 1.25x DSCR would support, at the note rate and on a 25-year amortization, is approximately $6.16 million — the Loan is roughly 2.4 times the amount the covenant supports. The rent roll workbook itself reaches the same conclusion and labels it "CRITICAL SHORTFALL."
[P]The consequence for drafting is direct. The first test date (month 24–27) coincides with the end of the interest-only period and the beginning of amortization, so the covenant will be tested at the moment debt service steps up by roughly 30%. Unless the loan is restructured, the Bank will hold a document that guarantees a default — which is exactly the outcome a covenant of this kind is meant to prevent, and which a borrower's counsel will characterize as evidence that the covenant was never a genuine term.
[1]**Recommendation:** Raise with Marcus Prideaux before the draft is delivered. The options, in order of my preference, are: (i) reduce the Loan amount or require a substantial principal paydown from lease-up proceeds; (ii) extend the interest-only period to month 36 and defer DSCR testing accordingly; (iii) set the covenant at a level the asset can meet (roughly 0.90x–1.00x on interest-only debt service at stabilization) with a cash sweep or DSCR cure deposit obligation; or (iv) retain 1.25x but add a defined DSCR cure right — a cash deposit or a letter of credit in the amount of the shortfall — so that a shortfall is a cure-and-collateral event rather than an immediate default. I have not selected among these; it is a credit decision for the Bank.
[H]**Issue 2 — "Annual Debt Service" is undefined in the term sheet, and the definition determines whether the covenant is capable of performance.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §7.1 ("The precise definitions of 'Net Operating Income' and 'Annual Debt Service' shall be set forth in the Loan Documents").
[P]The term sheet deliberately leaves both definitions open. I have drafted them in Section 1.1: NOI on a trailing twelve-month basis net of operating expenses but before debt service, capital expenditures, tenant improvements and leasing commissions; Annual Debt Service computed on the basis actually payable — interest-only during the Interest-Only Period and on the 25-year amortization thereafter. Those are the definitions most favorable to the Bank and they are the reason the covenant is unattainable. If the Bank prefers a covenant it can live with, the definition of Annual Debt Service is the lever: computing it on an interest-only equivalent basis raises every DSCR in the table above by about 30%.
[1]**Recommendation:** Confirm the definition with the Bank. Do not leave it to be negotiated by borrower's counsel after the other terms are settled, because it is a substantive credit term masquerading as a definitional one.
[H]**Issue 3 — Occupancy is misstated in the term sheet and the appraisal, and the error has propagated into the rent analysis.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §2.3; Appraisal §1 and §3.1; Rent Roll workbook, "Summary" tab.
[P]The term sheet and the appraisal both state current occupancy as 68%. The rent roll states 56.13%, and 56.13% is correct: three of five units are occupied, comprising Bay 1 (3,800 SF), Bay 3 (3,800 SF) and Suite A (9,800 SF), for 17,400 SF of 31,000 SF. The vacancy figure of 13,600 SF (Bay 2 and Suite B) is 43.87% of the building, and the term sheet itself recites that 43.9% vacancy figure two sentences after reciting 68% occupancy — the two statements cannot both be right. The appraisal is internally inconsistent in the same way: it states "68% (21,400 SF of 31,000 SF occupied)" and "vacant area is 13,600 SF (32%)," but 31,000 minus 13,600 is 17,400, and 13,600 divided by 31,000 is 43.87%, not 32%. The 21,400 SF figure appears to be the source of the error, and it also explains the appraisal's blended rent of $19.40/SF: $415,100 divided by 21,400 SF is $19.40, whereas divided by the correct 17,400 SF it is $23.86, which is the figure the rent roll states.
[P]This is not a drafting problem, but it is not a trivial one either. It affects the LTV and loan-to-cost commentary in the Bank's credit file, the 95% stabilized occupancy assumption, the absorption timeline, and any occupancy-based mechanic we might otherwise have drafted (a guaranty burn-off, a leasing covenant benchmark, or a release price). The Mortgage does not recite occupancy as a representation; Exhibit D states the correct 56.13% and 17,400 SF. I recommend the appraisal be corrected by addendum before it is placed in the credit file, and that the Bank's underwriting summary be conformed.
[1]**Recommendation:** Ask Pinnacle for a corrected addendum; confirm to Marcus that the occupancy in the appraisal is overstated by 4,000 SF; correct the term sheet file copy (the executed term sheet itself cannot be amended, but the credit file should carry a memo).
[H]**Issue 4 — The yield maintenance formula is ambiguous on four variables, and your suggested formula does not match the term sheet.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §§4.1–4.3; your markup notes, Section 5.
[P]The term sheet's formula is a "greater of" structure: (a) 1.00% of the outstanding principal balance at prepayment, or (b) the present value of the excess of interest at the note rate over interest at treasury plus 50 basis points, discounted at the treasury rate. You identified four open variables: the Treasury tenor, interpolation, the discount rate, and the treatment of a zero or negative result. I have resolved each in Section 4.5 in the manner you suggested — the Security shall be the H.15 yield to maturity of the Treasury issue maturing closest to but not exceeding the end of the Yield Maintenance Period, with linear interpolation, discounted monthly at the Treasury Rate divided by twelve, and a floor at the 1.00% minimum.
[P]Two points require your attention before it goes to the Bank. *First*, your suggested formula and the term sheet are not the same formula. Yours computes the present value of all remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest minus the principal prepaid; the term sheet computes a present-value interest differential against treasuries plus 50 basis points. The two produce different numbers in a rising rate environment — yours can be zero where the term sheet's is not, and vice versa — and the term sheet is the executed, binding document. I have followed the term sheet and used your language only for the defined variables. *Second*, your instruction that the premium shall "in no event be less than zero" is inconsistent with the term sheet's 1.00% minimum, which makes a zero result impossible. I have drafted the 1.00% minimum as controlling and retained the "not less than zero" sentence as a belt-and-braces statement that cannot operate to reduce the minimum. If you intended the zero floor to override the 1.00%, we need to say so expressly and explain to the Bank why we are giving up a bargained-for term.
[P]On the question you flagged — whether the 50 basis points is added to the loan rate or to the treasury rate — the term sheet is clear that it is added to the treasury rate ("the interest that would accrue on such prepaid principal amount at the treasury rate plus fifty (50) basis points"). Your note suggested the alternative. I have followed the term sheet. This should still be confirmed with Marcus, because if the Bank's intent was the other reading, the premium is materially larger and Borrower's counsel will resist a change after execution.
[1]**Also flagged:** the term sheet says the Loan "may not be prepaid" during the lockout (Section 4.1) but then says "any prepayment made in violation of this restriction shall be subject to a prepayment premium as described in Section 4.2" — which contemplates that such a prepayment can happen. I have drafted the lockout as an absolute prohibition with a right in Lender to refuse a tender, and a premium if Lender accepts one (Sections 4.3 and 4.7). I have also followed your instruction that casualty and condemnation proceeds are applied at par without premium; the term sheet does not address it, and you asked me to confirm it with the client. **This remains an open item.**
[H]**Issue 5 — The Guaranty is internally inconsistent, and the interest carry does not reach the DSCR problem.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §5.5(a)–(c).
[P]Section 5.5 is headed "full recourse personal guaranty" and then provides in (a) that "the Loan shall be structured as non-recourse to Borrower, except for certain 'carve-out' events." Those are different instruments, and the term sheet does not reconcile them. The Mortgage does not characterize the Guaranty's recourse (Section 14.15 describes the Borrower-level carve-outs and defers to the Guaranty Agreement for Guarantor), which keeps the Mortgage neutral. The Guaranty drafter needs a decision.
[P]Separately, Section 5.5(c) is a payment guaranty covering "any shortfall in debt service payments during the renovation and initial lease-up period, covering the first fourteen (14) months following closing." Fourteen months takes the guaranty to about June 2026 — before substantial completion, before the first DSCR test, and before amortization begins. On the figures in Issue 1, the interest shortfall is not a 14-month problem: in-place NOI of about $320,000 against annual interest of $862,875 leaves a shortfall of roughly $543,000 per year for as long as the vacancy persists, and stabilized NOI of about $587,000 still leaves a shortfall of roughly $276,000 per year even after full lease-up. The interest carry is therefore calibrated to the wrong period.
[1]**Recommendation:** If the Bank wants a guaranty that supports the loan while the property leases up, the interest carry should run from closing through the first DSCR test date (at least month 27, i.e., roughly 33 months), and should be measured against actual debt service including amortization, or converted into a DSCR guaranty. I have not drafted that; it is a Guaranty term, and I will draft it on instruction.
[H]**Issue 6 — Whether the assignment of rents is to be a separate instrument is unresolved in the term sheet.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §§5.2, 12.1(a), 14.3(b)–(c); Title Commitment Requirements 3 and 5.
[P]Section 5.2 permits the assignment to be included in the Mortgage "or executed as a separate instrument, at the discretion of Lender's counsel." Section 14.3(b)–(c) lists both a Mortgage and an Assignment of Leases and Rents among the documents "to be prepared and executed at closing," and describes the Assignment as "to be recorded, if prepared as a separate instrument." Title Commitment Requirement 5 accepts either. Following your instruction, I have integrated the absolute assignment into Article III and added Section 3.8, which obliges Borrower to execute a separate instrument if Lender later determines one is needed and requires recording of the Mortgage to perfect. That resolves the tension in the Bank's favor without adding a recording. But the closing index and the Loan Documents definition should be conformed so that the Bank's file does not show an undelivered document.
[1]**Note on citation:** your markup notes cite the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act at "S.C. Code § 29-3-100 et seq." My draft cites the Act by name with a Title 29, Chapter 3, Article 6 reference. The codification should be checked before the draft goes out — I have not verified the section numbers against the current Code.
[H]**Issue 7 — The term sheet contains no cash management, lockbox or DSCR cure mechanism, and the rent roll analysis recommends one.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet (absent); Rent Roll workbook, "Vacancy Schedule" tab, conclusion row.
[P]The term sheet requires an absolute assignment of rents but no deposit account control agreement, no cash management agreement, no lockbox and no cash sweep. Given the DSCR position described in Issue 1, that is a gap: the Bank's only cash remedy on default is to notify tenants, and its only credit protection is an unattainable covenant. The rent roll analysis recommends a cash sweep trigger at 1.10x and a DSCR cure deposit. I have not drafted any of those, because term sheet Section 14.4 permits additional provisions only where they are not materially inconsistent with the term sheet, and a cash management regime is a material commercial term that the Bank should elect. I have included only the assignment, the security interest in reserve accounts and a customary control agreement authorization (Section 10.4).
[1]**Recommendation:** Put the question to Marcus together with Issue 1. If the Bank elects cash management, it will require a separate agreement and an amendment to the Loan Documents list.
EOF

[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §§4.1–4.3; your markup notes, Section 5.
[P]The term sheet's formula is a "greater of" structure: (a) 1.00% of the outstanding principal balance at prepayment, or (b) the present value of the excess of interest at the note rate over interest at treasury plus 50 basis points, discounted at the treasury rate. You identified four open variables: the Treasury tenor, interpolation, the discount rate, and the treatment of a zero or negative result. I have resolved each in Section 4.5 in the manner you suggested — the Security shall be the H.15 yield to maturity of the Treasury issue maturing closest to but not exceeding the end of the Yield Maintenance Period, with linear interpolation, discounted monthly at the Treasury Rate divided by twelve, and a floor at the 1.00% minimum.
[P]Two points require your attention before it goes to the Bank. *First*, your suggested formula and the term sheet are not the same formula. Yours computes the present value of all remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest minus the principal prepaid; the term sheet computes a present-value interest differential against treasuries plus 50 basis points. The two produce different numbers in a rising rate environment — yours can be zero where the term sheet's is not, and vice versa — and the term sheet is the executed, binding document. I have followed the term sheet and used your language only for the defined variables. *Second*, your instruction that the premium shall "in no event be less than zero" is inconsistent with the term sheet's 1.00% minimum, which makes a zero result impossible. I have drafted the 1.00% minimum as controlling and retained the "not less than zero" sentence as a belt-and-braces statement that cannot operate to reduce the minimum. If you intended the zero floor to override the 1.00%, we need to say so expressly and explain to the Bank why we are giving up a bargained-for term.
[P]On the question you flagged — whether the 50 basis points is added to the loan rate or to the treasury rate — the term sheet is clear that it is added to the treasury rate ("the interest that would accrue on such prepaid principal amount at the treasury rate plus fifty (50) basis points"). Your note suggested the alternative. I have followed the term sheet. This should still be confirmed with Marcus, because if the Bank's intent was the other reading, the premium is materially larger and Borrower's counsel will resist a change after execution.
[1]**Also flagged:** the term sheet says the Loan "may not be prepaid" during the lockout (Section 4.1) but then says "any prepayment made in violation of this restriction shall be subject to a prepayment premium as described in Section 4.2" — which contemplates that such a prepayment can happen. I have drafted the lockout as an absolute prohibition with a right in Lender to refuse a tender, and a premium if Lender accepts one (Sections 4.3 and 4.7). I have also followed your instruction that casualty and condemnation proceeds are applied at par without premium; the term sheet does not address it, and you asked me to confirm it with the client. **This remains an open item.**
[H]**Issue 5 — The Guaranty is internally inconsistent, and the interest carry does not reach the DSCR problem.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §5.5(a)–(c).
[P]Section 5.5 is headed "full recourse personal guaranty" and then provides in (a) that "the Loan shall be structured as non-recourse to Borrower, except for certain 'carve-out' events." Those are different instruments, and the term sheet does not reconcile them. The Mortgage does not characterize the Guaranty's recourse (Section 14.15 describes the Borrower-level carve-outs and defers to the Guaranty Agreement for Guarantor), which keeps the Mortgage neutral. The Guaranty drafter needs a decision.
[P]Separately, Section 5.5(c) is a payment guaranty covering "any shortfall in debt service payments during the renovation and initial lease-up period, covering the first fourteen (14) months following closing." Fourteen months takes the guaranty to about June 2026 — before substantial completion, before the first DSCR test, and before amortization begins. On the figures in Issue 1, the interest shortfall is not a 14-month problem: in-place NOI of about $320,000 against annual interest of $862,875 leaves a shortfall of roughly $543,000 per year for as long as the vacancy persists, and stabilized NOI of about $587,000 still leaves a shortfall of roughly $276,000 per year even after full lease-up. The interest carry is therefore calibrated to the wrong period.
[1]**Recommendation:** If the Bank wants a guaranty that supports the loan while the property leases up, the interest carry should run from closing through the first DSCR test date (at least month 27, i.e., roughly 33 months), and should be measured against actual debt service including amortization, or converted into a DSCR guaranty. I have not drafted that; it is a Guaranty term, and I will draft it on instruction.
[H]**Issue 6 — Whether the assignment of rents is to be a separate instrument is unresolved in the term sheet.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet §§5.2, 12.1(a), 14.3(b)–(c); Title Commitment Requirements 3 and 5.
[P]Section 5.2 permits the assignment to be included in the Mortgage "or executed as a separate instrument, at the discretion of Lender's counsel." Section 14.3(b)–(c) lists both a Mortgage and an Assignment of Leases and Rents among the documents "to be prepared and executed at closing," and describes the Assignment as "to be recorded, if prepared as a separate instrument." Title Commitment Requirement 5 accepts either. Following your instruction, I have integrated the absolute assignment into Article III and added Section 3.8, which obliges Borrower to execute a separate instrument if Lender later determines one is needed and requires recording of the Mortgage to perfect. That resolves the tension in the Bank's favor without adding a recording. But the closing index and the Loan Documents definition should be conformed so that the Bank's file does not show an undelivered document.
[1]**Note on citation:** your markup notes cite the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act at "S.C. Code § 29-3-100 et seq." My draft cites the Act by name with a Title 29, Chapter 3, Article 6 reference. The codification should be checked before the draft goes out — I have not verified the section numbers against the current Code.
[H]**Issue 7 — The term sheet contains no cash management, lockbox or DSCR cure mechanism, and the rent roll analysis recommends one.**
[1]**Source:** Term Sheet (absent); Rent Roll workbook, "Vacancy Schedule" tab, conclusion row.
[P]The term sheet requires an absolute assignment of rents but no deposit account control agreement, no cash management agreement, no lockbox and no cash sweep. Given the DSCR position described in Issue 1, that is a gap: the Bank's only cash remedy on default is to notify tenants, and its only credit protection is an unattainable covenant. The rent roll analysis recommends a cash sweep trigger at 1.10x and a DSCR cure deposit. I have not drafted any of those, because term sheet Section 14.4 permits additional provisions only where they are not materially inconsistent with the term sheet, and a cash management regime is a material commercial term that the Bank should elect. I have included only the assignment, the security interest in reserve accounts and a customary control agreement authorization (Section 10.4).
[1]**Recommendation:** Put the question to Marcus together with Issue 1. If the Bank elects cash management, it will require a separate agreement and an amendment to the Loan Documents list.

[P]The title commitment shows fee simple title vested in Hampstead Village Holdings LLC by virtue of a general warranty deed recorded September 14, 2018 in Deed Book 1095 at Page 322. Title passes to Borrower only on recording of the deed contemplated by Requirement 2(a). The Mortgage must therefore be executed and recorded by Borrower after the deed is recorded — and the recording sequence matters, because a mortgage given by a person who is not yet the record owner creates a priority and enforceability question that the title insurer will not resolve for us. The Mortgage recites the acquisition in Recital B and represents in Section 5.3 that Borrower "will, upon recording of the deed described in Section 6.8 and immediately prior to the recording of this Mortgage, be the sole fee simple owner" — a formulation that is true when made and at closing. [H]**Issue 9 — The Anson Lane strip was conveyed by quitclaim deed only, and the description of it in the term sheet is incomplete.**
[1]**Source:** Title Commitment, Schedule A §3, Schedule A §4 (Parcel Two), and Notes to Closer ¶3; Term Sheet §2.1 and Exhibit A; your markup notes, Section 2.
[P]I have worked through the three verification steps in your notes as far as the record permits. *First*, the commitment does insure the strip: Schedule A §3 recites vesting of the strip in Hampstead Village Holdings LLC by quitclaim deed recorded March 22, 2019 in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, and Schedule A §4 includes it as Parcel Two. Term Sheet §2.1 and Exhibit A describe Parcel Two only by reference to the quitclaim deed; they omit the recorded plat reference to the Cartwright Land Surveying LLC plat dated January 15, 2025, recorded in Plat Book 64 at Page 91, which is how the title commitment describes the strip. **Exhibit A to the Mortgage uses the title commitment's description**, which includes both. [1]**Source:** Term Sheet §2.1 and Exhibit A; Title Commitment Schedule A §4 and Requirement 9; your markup notes, Section 2.
